News.title: Ukraine's desperate appeal for US Patriot defence missiles before winter arrives
News.content:
Ukraine's desperate appeal for US Patriot defence missiles before winter arrives

President Zelensky appeals to the US for more Patriots pre-winter as Kyiv predicts Puntin will once again weaponise plummeting temperatures and try to freeze civilians to death

View 4 Images Kyiv under attack by Russian forces this week (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Ukraine has made a desperate appeal to US President Donald Trump sell it up to 10% of its badly-needed Patriot defence missiles before winter. President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine could destroy all of the Kremlin’s deadly ballistic missiles and save lives with just 10% of the US Patriots.

‌



Last night Russian forces launched 133 drones at Ukraine, hitting 15 locations and killing two more civilians in Odesa and wounding five in Dnipropetrovsk region and another in Zaporizhzhia. Zelensky is keen to acquire Patriots before winter as Russia will likely weaponise the bitter cold by targeting civilian energy supplies.

‌



But it is widely-reported the US has depleted its Patriot stocks by up to a third throughout its five month war with Iran, defending against Tehran’s firepower.

‌



View 4 Images Another Russian ballistic missile attack on Zaporizhzhia (Image: Ukrinform/Shutterstock)

Trump will never secure deal and Iran will wait out warning, claims Tehran insider READ MORE :

And American weapons manufacturers have been told to speed up production of the Patriots, which are usually produced at a rate of around 650 a-year. President Zelensky said: "This year I’m asking American partners to sell me five per cent of missiles, what they have in their stocks.

‌



"If they sell us five per cent we will go through the winter and save people’s lives. If they can sell us 10%, we will destroy all the Russians’ ballistic missiles.” In July, Ukraine intercepted just 29 of the 195 ballistic missiles fired by Vladimir Putin ’s military - many of them at civilians. Last month was the deadliest for Ukraine’s civilians since the full-scale invasion was launched in 2022.

View 4 Images Russian leader President Vladimir Putin (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

At least 437 civilians were killed and 2,610 injured in Ukraine in July, a 30 per cent increase compared with the previous month and a 70 per cent increase compared with July 2025. Zelensky argued: “Russia has two times more ballistic missiles per month than they had before.” It is believed Moscow is producing 1,000 ballistic missiles a-year and now it is stepping up production and also buying in North Korean missiles.

Article continues below

At least 12 people were killed earlier this week by Pyongyang-made ballistic missiles. And Ukrainian intelligence reports claim that Russia's monthly production of key missiles is running up to 20% above target. Danielle Bell, head of the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission, said of the Ukrainian casualties: “Every month this year the number of killed and injured civilians has increased.

View 4 Images Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky (Image: Jemal Countess/UPI/REX/Shutterstock)

“That trend accelerated sharply in July. The number of civilian casualties in July was the highest we documented in a single month since March 2022.” Russia has suffered 1.4 losses of frontline troops to death or injury since war began, according to Ukraine. And Ukrainian forces have recently retaken 26 settlements and pushed Russian troops back across at least six areas of the frontline. The counter-attacks, led by air assault soldiers, have won back roughly 700 square miles of territory for Ukraine.

News.title: Heatwave sees NHS England’s top doctor issue urgent warning to stay safe today
News.content:
Heatwave sees NHS England’s top doctor issue urgent warning to stay safe today

NHS data shows the waiting list fell last month while A&Es have come under record pressure during multiple heatwaves - as temperatures could hit 38C today

View 3 Images Professor Frankie Swords has issued urgent advice

NHS England’s top doctor has warned people to stay safe today as new data shows how the health service is coping with the sweltering heat.

‌



A&Es saw a record 2.5 million attendances last month amid two heatwaves with new NHS data showing the three busiest months ever recorded were from May to July. The NHS elective waiting list in England has fallen for the first time in two months. Temperatures could hit as high as 38C in places today as Britain is in the grip of the fifth heatwave of the summer.

‌



Professor Frankie Swords, NHS National Medical Director, said: "With temperatures peaking today, please take sensible precautions to stay safe: keep hydrated, avoid the sun during the hottest part of the day especially if you are clinically vulnerable, and check in on older or vulnerable friends, relatives and neighbours.

‌



View 3 Images Prof Swords advises people to avoid the sun during the hottest part of the day (Image: Ben Whitley/PA Wire)

UK heatwaves warning as nearly 3,000 people dead in just two months of hot weather READ MORE :

Heatwaves saw 2,700 extra deaths in UK with 29 drowned READ MORE :

"While the NHS is busy, it is here for anyone who needs it, so please continue to call 999 in a life-threatening emergency and otherwise use NHS 111."

The elective waiting list for planned appointments edged down by 6,093 in June to 7.27 million – down from 7.28m in May. The backlog remains higher than at the start of the year but has dropped by around 100,000 patients compared to the same month last year.

‌



The NHS normally sees increases in A&E attendees in the summer but health chiefs say this year has seen unprecedented pressure. More people are involved in activities outdoors while breathing conditions can be worsened by high temperatures.

Some 75.4% of patients in England were seen within four hours in A&Es last month, up from 75.0% in June. The number of people waiting more than 12 hours in emergency departments - from a decision to admit to actually being admitted - stood at 47,438, down from 49,466.

Professor Swords added: "Like many members of the public, NHS staff are enjoying the lovely weather outside of work, but the heat is making day-to-day working more challenging while also driving up pressure on services. But staff are as ever demonstrating outstanding professionalism, flexibility and hard work in the face of this summer surge.”

‌



The NHS elective waiting list in England had been on an upward trend for a decade under previous Conservative governments. The backlog passed three million treatments in 2014, four million in 2017, five million in 2021 and peaked at 7.8 million in 2023 before Labour came to power in 2024.

View 3 Images Scorched earth at Maiden Castle Iron Age hillfort in Dorchester (Image: Getty Images)

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said: "I want to thank NHS staff for their extraordinary efforts over this hugely challenging summer.

Article continues below

"Despite the extreme heat and record demand that NHS staff have faced, more than three quarters of patients were seen within four hours in A&E, a record 2.65 million diagnostic tests and checks were carried out in a single month, and the waiting list has fallen in the month of June for the first time since 2011.

“Today's figures also show how much of an additional burden is placed on the NHS during periods of extreme heat, and I have made clear that we must start planning for summer pressures in the NHS in the same way we do for winter.

"That’s why I'm working closely with NHS leaders to put those plans in place, and ensure that our staffing, beds and emergency services are prepared for the demand we know is likely to come, and that our health service can keep delivering for patients, no matter the weather."

News.title: Birmingham Pride under fire for tickets prices after bosses pledged to make event free
News.content:
Birmingham Pride under fire for tickets prices after bosses pledged to make event free

Birmingham Pride has faced backlash for their 2027 ticket prices - which start from £29 - after bosses seemingly scrapped earlier plans to make the event free to attend

View 2 Images Festival director Lawrence Barton hoped to make the event free to attend

Birmingham Pride is under fire after plans to make the event free to attend were seemingly scrapped, as ticket prices for 2027 are revealed. The event is set to celebrate its 30th anniversary, a moment bosses hoped to mark by removing ticket fees altogether.

‌



In April, festival director Lawrence Barton revealed his hopes to make the festival entirely free for its 30th anniversary in 2027 and declared his intention to "hand the baton" to another organiser to take Pride into the future if he pulls it off.

‌



Talking to BirminghamLive, Lawrence said: "In 1997 I attended the first Birmingham Pride, 2027 will be the 30th anniversary. I’d love to bring it full circle. In my own mind, I’d love for it to be a free festival."

‌



Lawrence added that security concerns, as well as the costs involved in road closures, clean-up operations, artist hire, security and infrastructure, meant there was a balance to be struck when organising, but confirmed that a free pride event was possible and that he intended to push forward with the plan, navigating any challenges along the way.

View 2 Images Birmingham Pride tickets start from £29

The annual parade is free-to-attend and then it is followed by a two-day ticketed celebration in the village with performers and artists set across multiple stages and venues. Performers include Katy B, Sigala, Nadine of Girls Aloud fame, Bjorn Again, Boney M ft Maizie Williams and Danny Beard.

‌



This year, prices were slashed significantly amid cost of living crisis concerns and in a bid to make the event more accessible. For 2027, prices start from £29.51 and can be purchased here, while more costly tickets go up to £110.

Commenters shared their thoughts under a Birmingham Pride announcement post on Facebook, with one writing: "So free festival in 2027 lasted about 5 minutes." Another chimed in, adding: "Thought pride was going to be free next year".

Birmingham Pride replied: "We have previously spoken about our aspiration to explore a free Pride, and we completely understand why people may have been looking forward to that.

‌



"As we have developed our plans for our 30th anniversary, we have carefully considered what is needed to deliver a Pride that is safe, accessible, diverse, affordable and sustainable, while retaining the elements that make Birmingham Pride so special.

"For 2027, we've decided that the best way to achieve that is through our full festival programme, alongside our Big Free Community Event on Friday, affordable loyalty tickets and our Low-Income Ticket Scheme, which will offer eligible people tickets at 50% of face value. We know affordability matters, and it's something we remain absolutely committed to."

Some were onboard with Birmingham Pride's pricing, with one arguing: "You can’t have a free pride with the big acts they have because they don’t come cheap regardless I’ll be happy to always pay for pride with good acts! Also they put so much into the community all year round."

Article continues below

The Mirror has reached out to Birmingham Pride for further comment.

News.title: Met chief accepts mistakes made over Simon Levy but defends investigation into murders
News.content:
The head of the Metropolitan Police Sir Mark Rowley has defended the force's investigation into double murderer Simon Levy.

Levy was on bail and being monitored by police when he murdered Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo in March 2025 and Sheryl Wilkins five months later, as well as violently raping a third woman.

Sir Mark acknowledged mistakes over the force's handling of Levy, but said suggestions it had not tried to build a case over his first murder were "just not true", following criticism including from Labour MP Jess Phillips.

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that detectives had done "serious" work but "didn't have enough evidence" for a charge.

The Met did not seek a charging decision from the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) over Valencia-Trujillo's murder until after Wilkins had been killed.

The police and CPS has apologised over a series of decisions that left the convicted sex offender free to attack the women.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is currently examining how Levy, 40, was managed over the four-year period from his first conviction in September 2021 for sexual assault up to his final arrest in September 2025.

At the Old Bailey on Wednesday, he was given a whole life prison sentence, meaning he will never be released.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Sir Mark - who on Wednesday called the case a "whole system failing" - said he had already apologised for what the Met had got wrong.

It emerged after Levy's conviction that the Met did not class Valencia-Trujillo's death in March 2025 as a murder, or pass the case to specialist homicide detectives, until after he had killed again.

But Sir Mark said "the public debate needs to be better informed" because "the facts on that are much more complex than people want to acknowledge".

He said that while Valencia-Trujillo's death was "clearly very suspicious and concerning", a pathologist was unable to determine a cause of death and the force "didn't have enough evidence to get to a charge".

Sir Mark added it was only after the murder of Wilkins that the Met had the "combined evidence" to move forward.

"So the inference that the Met didn't try on that case is just not true, the Met tried," he said.

However, the Met did not ask the CPS for advice about Valencia-Trujillo's death, let alone a charging decision, until after the murder of Wilkins, the BBC has previously reported.

The fact there was no formal cause of death would not have prevented the case being taken on by specialist homicide detectives, who are skilled at building murder cases even when there is not a formal cause of death.

Levy's semen was on Valencia-Trujillo and his blood was at the murder scene. CCTV that showed Levy in the area, walking in the same direction as Valencia-Trujillo shortly after she passed a camera, was not viewed by the local team despite being gathered.

Other possible relevant CCTV was never gathered, and had been deleted by the time the specialist murder team took over months later.

In that case, the local team investigating the death did not engage with the Met's specialist murder teams apart from the day her body was discovered in March 2025.

A specialist homicide team attended the crime scene that day and recommended the case stay with local officers pending further enquiries, but there was no further contact until after Wilkins was murdered in August.

News.title: Water bills set to rise for many after firms permitted extra funding
News.content:
Water companies have been given a provisional green light to increase bills for customers by an extra Â£3.4bn in coming years to meet increased pressures on infrastructure and the environment.

Nearly a third of the extra funding for 13 water companies in England and Wales is earmarked for ensuring water services are maintained.

Further sums are set to meet rising demand from housebuilding and data centres and to address pollutants known as "forever chemicals".

But a group campaigning for better water quality in the UK's rivers described the decision as "an insult".

The regulator, Ofwat, said the extra spending would enable the firms to support growth and better environmental outcomes and ensure important upgrades were not delayed.

"We will track performance to ensure companies are delivering the expected improvements for customers and the environment," said Helen Campbell, executive director for delivery at Ofwat.

"If they don't, expenditure can be clawed back."

Water companies need approval from the regulator, Ofwat, to raise customers' bills, a process that takes place every five years to set spending budgets for the years ahead.

This decision to allow increased charges comes on top of already-agreed bill rises that were negotiated with the water companies in 2024.

The process allows firms to apply for additional funds for projects that were not known about at the time of the last review.

As part of the outlined increase, Ofwat has approved funding for schemes including provision for new data centres in Manchester, additional wastewater capacity in Newquay and to bring forward work by Wessex Water to tackle PFAS, originally planned for 2030-35.

However, the decision is provisional. There is a period of public consultation, with a final decision due in December.

Some of the additional spending would be recovered through customer bills before the end of this decade, some would come after 2030.

Bills will rise for customers of five of the 13 water companies before 2030: customers of Severn Trent Water, Southern Water, Thames Water, Wessex Water, and South East Water will experience price rises of Â£1 to Â£43 in the 2027/28 and 2029/30 financial years..

Ofwat said water companies had submitted a total of Â£4.3bn worth of requests, but some of their proposed extra spending had been rejected.

River Action's head of campaigns Amy Fairman said: "Ofwat waving through yet more water bill hikes is an insult."

Water companies had failed to make sufficient investment over the last 30 years, she said, leaving customers with "leaks, pollution and soaring bills".

There should be greater public control of water companies, she added. "No more blank cheques for failure."

News.title: Watch: Key moments from Karoline Leavitt's White House tenure as Trump says she will leave post
News.content:
White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will step down from her role at the end of August to spend time with her young children and family, after welcoming her second child in May.

"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party," President Donald Trump wrote in a social media post announcing her departure.

Leavitt became the youngest press secretary in the country's history when she took the job in January 2025 at age 27.

News.title: Scientists invent 'world's greenest party balloon'
News.content:
Scientists in London have invented what they claim is the world's first fully biodegradable party balloon.

Researchers at Imperial College London say standard balloons can take years to break down and can release harmful chemicals.

But their new balloon biodegrades within nine months.

The research was part-funded by a party planner, who wanted to reduce the impact of balloon litter on marine wildlife.

The new balloon, called Bioloon, is no more expensive than a standard balloon and is easier to blow up, according to the scientists.

"Regular balloons are treated with a process to make them strong and stretchy," said 29-year-old co-inventor Juliana Cumming, a PhD researcher at Imperial. "But that process also stops them fully degrading and causes toxic chemicals to leach into the environment."

News.title: Once-in-a-generation solar eclipse wows millions in UK and Europe
News.content:
The UK and Europe have enjoyed their most dramatic solar eclipse for nearly 30 years, with millions thought to have witnessed the once-in-a-generation event.

Those watching the astronomical phenomenon from the UK were treated to a partial eclipse, which peaked shortly after 19:00 BST, when most saw more than 90% of the Sun covered by the Moon.

But parts of Greenland, Iceland and Spain experienced the complete darkness and spectacle of a total eclipse.

Large crowds at viewing sites across the UK and Europe reacted with gasps and cheers, with astronomy enthusiasts saying it served as a reminder of how "amazing" the Universe is.

News.title: UK economy grows but experts warn of challenging months ahead
News.content:
Summer sun and sports fixtures helped the UK economy grow between April and June, according to official data, but some economists warned the outlook for the rest of the year was weaker.

The economy expanded by 0.4%, in line with market expectations but below a 0.6% increase in the first three months of this year.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said growth had "remained relatively robust", with the UK ahead of other G7 countries for growth this year so far.

Experts questioned whether this resilience would be maintained, however, given growth was fuelled by some temporary factors and energy prices could remain volatile if the Middle East conflict continues.

The British economy is now 1.2% bigger than a year ago, the ONS said, despite fears that the Iran war, which started at the end of February, and politically uncertainty around Sir Keir Starmer's resignation as prime minister would hold back growth.

Between April and June, sectors including computer programming, advertising and the pharmaceutical industry lifted growth. That was offset by falls in power generation and sewerage.

The ONS said some businesses reported that "good weather and sporting events may have had a positive effect" in June, boosting month-on-month growth to 0.3%.

The men's football World Cup, which kicked off mid-June, increased customers at hospitality venues showing the matches.

June also saw several of summer's heatwaves. However, May's growth was revised down from 0.1% to zero growth.

News.title: Polls open in Clacton by-election
News.content:
The polls have opened in Clacton-on-Sea as a record number of candidates vie to become the town's next MP.

An electorate of 79,785 registered voters have the chance to vote for one of 34 candidates standing in the Essex resort - the most ever to stand in a British election.

Fifty-one polling stations have opened, covering Clacton and the surrounding towns of Jaywick, Frinton and Walton-on-the-Naze. The constituency also has rural villages including St Osyth, Weeley and Great Bentley.

Voters will need to show a form of acceptable ID - such as a driving licence or passport - to be able to cast their ballot.

They will receive the longest ballot paper in British electoral history at 90cm - about 3ft long - to choose their candidate and cast their vote.

There are 12 political parties and 20 independents standing.

Polling stations will remain open to anyone registered to vote until 22:00, with the count taking place overnight.

News.title: Results, appeals and resits - what to do if things don't go to plan
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland have opened their A-level, T-level and BTec results.

They were released at 08:00 BST on Thursday 13 August.

Those who have applied to university should be able to see whether they have been successful too, as the Ucas Hub updates at the same time.

Here is everything you need to know about results, appeals and resits.

News.title: Leading doctor rebukes NHS chiefs over transplant failings
News.content:
While NHS Blood and Transplant manages organ donations and supports transplant centres, services are commissioned and paid for by NHS England.

But in a letter to NHS England and a small group of patient advocates, Manas said the central body had created a "fragmented" system "with poor accountability".

There is a "mismatch", he said, between each hospital's waiting lists, organ availability, capacity to carry out surgeries and the availability of operating theatres.

This is "leading to last-minute cancellations [and] unpredictable utilisation of donated organs," he warned.

The BBC reported in March that the UK, once a world leader, had fallen behind major Western nations in heart and lung transplantation, though it fares better in other areas such as kidney transplantation.

The NHS transplants one in 10 lungs and one in seven hearts that are donated - half the proportions seen in some other countries.

It has not invested in modern technology at the same rate as other countries, and suffers from a lack of theatre space, intensive care beds and staff.

Wales and Northern Ireland do not have a heart and lung transplant centre, so patients commonly travel to England for surgery. There is one heart transplant centre in Scotland.

News.title: Farm show bans cattle and sheep amid outbreak
News.content:
Some 353 cases of bluetongue serotype 3 (BTV3) have been recorded in the UK in the 2026/27 season - most of them in the south-west of England.

The virus is spread by insects and is generally found in cattle, sheep and goats. It does not affect people or food safety but it causes a high rate of death in infected sheep and fertility problems in infected cattle.

Barrow said the team had been working closely with vets ahead of the show.

"We've worked through lots of different scenarios as to ways that we could keep the cattle and sheep and goat sections going, such as only bringing vaccinated sheep or putting on a really reduced, very local show.

"But, we thought because the situation is ever-changing and the volume of cases was just increasing exponentially, that the best thing for us to do for this year was to withdraw our cattle sheep in eight sections."

"We felt because we have a big cattle and sheep section, that bringing people in from quite far out of area, just wouldn't have been the best thing for us to do while it's still a new and emerging situation, and we're still learning all about it," she added.

Organisers of the Launceston Agricultural Show took the same decision in July regarding cattle and sheep.

News.title: Three teenagers guilty of man's murder and robbery
News.content:
Three teenagers on a violent mission "to obtain money or drugs" have been found guilty of murdering a man.

The body of David Cuthbert, 49, was discovered at a house in Egglescliffe Close, in Stockton, on 10 January.

Layton Lightfoot and Jesse Reaney, both 18, and Charlie Wilcock, 19, were convicted of murder and robbery following a trial at Teesside Crown Court on Wednesday.

Lightfoot, of Stockwith Close in Middlesbrough, Reaney, of Lowthian Road in Hartlepool, and Wilcock, of no fixed address, are due to be sentenced on 27 November.

Det Supt Daryll Tomlinson, of Cleveland Police, said the three defendants were "heavily involved in criminality" and had sought to "assert their authority" and "brazenly brag about their violence to those online".

He said: "[They] were on a mission that day to use violence through the use of weapons to obtain money or drugs from those living within the community."

News.title: Man jailed over one-punch death after pub row
News.content:
A man who fatally punched a fellow regular at a pub in a row over a phone charger has been jailed for five years after being convicted of manslaughter.

Harry Mannion, 28, punched 62-year-old Tony Powles to the ground during a row at the Red Lion on Batley Road in Wakefield on 9 October.

Powles, a father-of-four who was due to marry his partner the following week, suffered a "catastrophic brain injury" when he hit his head on the floor and died 13 days later, Leeds Crown Court heard.

In a victim impact statement, his daughter Rebecca Powles described him as the "absolute pillar of our family", adding: "He had so many friends and was loved by absolutely everyone who knew him."

Rebecca Powles said the family had been "forced to suffer beyond the boundaries of normal grief", telling the court: "We will never, ever forget having to make the excruciating decision to turn off his life support."

Mannion, himself a father of a five-year-old daughter, had denied manslaughter - claiming to have acted in self-defence - but was found guilty following a trial in June.

The court heard how the pair were both regulars at the Red Lion and had been "pub friends".

At the time Mannion, from Barnsley, was in a relationship with the pub's manager, while Powles had gone there that evening with his family.

Tensions arose when the defendant "took a dim view" of one of Powles's daughters serving behind the bar as part of her training to work there, prosecutor Matthew Harding said.

Later, Mannion was said to have taken exception to Powles's sister, Linda Wilson, using a phone charger belonging to him which had been behind the bar.

An argument ensued and Wilson left the bar.

When Powles found out about the disagreement, CCTV footage showed him approach Mannion at the bar, "when words were exchanged", said Judge Simon Phillips KC.

Powles then threw the charger, catching Mannion on the side of his head, before headbutting him.

About a minute later, when Powles was being restrained with his hands by his side, Mannion "threw a forceful punch at [the victim's] head", Judge Phillips said.

"This was retaliation from you, done in drink, from what had gone on moments before," Judge Phillips told the defendant, who appeared in court via video link from HMP Leeds.

News.title: Residents' 'absolute fear' as massive fire destroyed their homes
News.content:
People preparing to watch the eclipse were instead witness to a massive fire that destroyed homes and left 20 people evacuated to a leisure centre, a councillor in south Wales has said.

There are no reports of casualties, but six bungalows were evacuated near Hazelwood Road, Newbridge, in Caerphilly county, on Wednesday.

"Everyone was getting ready yesterday to witness the eclipse, and for this to happen last night was a total shock," said councillor Gary Johnston.

Julia Nichols, 74, was one of the people evacuated from her home and said the fire left her in "absolute fear".

News.title: Man dies days after explosion at bungalow
News.content:
A man has died in hospital days after a suspected gas explosion at a bungalow.

The blast, which happened at 09:45 BST on Sunday, destroyed the home on Cobb Hall Road in Newton Longville, a village near Milton Keynes.

Thames Valley Police said a man in his 60s was taken to hospital where he was receiving treatment for his injuries. His death was announced on Thursday.

He has been named as Steve Woodward in a tribute post by Newton Longville Parish Council and in a fundraising page set up in the aftermath of the explosion.

Det Insp Philip Turner-Robson said: "This is a tragic development and our thoughts are with the man's family and friends at this extremely difficult time.

"Thames Valley Police is managing a coronial investigation into the circumstances surrounding the explosion and collapse of the property, working jointly with the Health and Safety Executive.

"Our inquiries remain ongoing as we seek to establish the full circumstances of what happened."

News.title: Arrest in Thetford migrant address sharing investigation
News.content:
Police have arrested a man as part of an inquiry into how the addresses of asylum seekers were shared during disorder linked to anti-immigration protests in a town, the BBC can reveal.

Properties in St John's Way, Bracken Road, Clover Way, Elm Road and Chester Way in Thetford, Norfolk, were recently targeted by crowds over three nights.

The man, in his 60s, was arrested on Friday on suspicion of assisting an offender and inciting racial hatred and has been released on bail until 14 October.

The houses are believed to have been used by Serco, a firm contracted to accommodate migrants, which said it was investigating allegations "relating to how address information has been made public".

The firm added it was working with the Home Office and Norfolk Police "to ensure that appropriate safeguarding measures are in place".

After his arrest, the man in his 60s was taken to Wymondham Police Investigation Centre for questioning.

News.title: 'Online trolls who target me are bored and jealous'
News.content:
A woman who posts food reviews on social media has spoken out against the level of online abuse she receives after some trolls have urged her to take her own life.

Gloucestershire's Becca Stock, who has millions of followers on TikTok, said while "bored" and "jealous" people do target her online, they are in the minority.

She has shared her experience of online bullying following the University of Gloucestershire publishing new research into what drives digital abuse.

Dr Amy Grubb, associate professor of forensic psychology at the University, said posting comments online creates the "perfect storm" for abuse as the "digital environments reduce normal social restraints".

The research comes as mental health charities are reporting that online harms are having a growing impact on young people's wellbeing.

The number of school leavers in the UK accepted onto degree courses has risen to a record high this year.

A total of 262,820 UK 18-year-olds have gained a place at university or college – up 3 per cent on the same point last year, according to data published by the university admissions service.

Ucas said it is the highest number of placed students on results day on record, driven by a rising number of 18-year-olds in the population.

The overall number of students, of all ages and domiciles, being accepted has also reached a record high – with 446,690 successful applicants up from 439,180 last year.

Hundreds of thousands of students across England, Wales and Northern Ireland are receiving grades to help them decide whether to progress to university, an apprenticeship or work.

Results day comes amid a crisis in the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet).

Students celebrate A-level, BTEC and T-level results at Oaklands College, 13 August 2026 ( Oaklands College )

The Department for Education estimates that nearly 58,000 18-year-olds in England will get no results on Thursday because they have dropped out of education and training, although some are working.

The latest data, published in May, showed the number of young people aged 16 to 24 neither working nor learning surpassed one million for the first time since 2013, reaching 1.01 million in the three months from January to March.

The education secretary said she is focused on a “revolution” in technical and vocational pathways to answer the “clarion call” of the Neets crisis.

In a statement ahead of results day, Lucy Powell said: “My priority is making sure every young person has the skills, knowledge, and confidence to thrive in the jobs of the future.

“That’s why we’re giving technical education the respect it deserves by rolling out new V Levels to go alongside A Levels, introducing brilliant routes into the careers of the future from age 14, and fully funding apprenticeship training for under-25s.”

For many students, receiving their exam results on Thursday will also bring confirmation of university places.

On the day before A-level results day, a sample of 131 of the UK’s largest higher education providers showed there were 22,698 courses with vacancies for undergraduate students living in England on the Ucas clearing site – which matches applicants to university places yet to be filled.

Eighteen of the 24 Russell Group universities, which represent some of the most selective UK institutions, had vacancies on courses for English residents – a total of 3,483 courses between them.

Solar panel installations are surging across the UK, according to official data, with new figures showing that 2026 could be another record-breaking year for households generating their own electricity.

More homeowners are investing in the best solar panels available, as they look to cut their reliance on grid electricity and take greater control of their energy bills.

According to the latest government figures cited by energy supplier E.ON Next, 142,536 solar installations were added across the UK during the first six months of 2026, taking the total number to more than 2 million.

These figures put the UK on course to surpass the record for solar installations set just last year.

E.ON Next has also reported an even sharper increase among its customers, stating that solar installations rose by 151 per cent during the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025.

Get a quote for solar panels for your home

Use our comparison tool to get free quotes from leading solar panel installers.

Why are more homeowners installing solar panels?

The latest increase follows a record year for the technology. According to the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), 269,000 solar installations were completed in 2025. This was 37 per cent more than in 2024, making 2025 the highest calendar year on record for solar installations.

Around 255,000 of these were rooftop systems, meaning at least 95 per cent of installations were on homes, businesses and other buildings rather than standalone solar farms.

One factor making solar more accessible is falling upfront costs. Government figures published in May showed the cost of acquiring and installing solar PV had fallen by up to 9 per cent, depending on the size of the system.

For households considering making the switch, comparing quotes from the best solar panel installers can help establish the likely upfront cost, the number of panels a property needs and the potential savings.

Solar panels can reduce the amount of electricity a household needs to buy from the grid by supplying power directly to the home. Surplus electricity can also be stored in a solar battery for later use or exported to the grid through a Smart Export Guarantee tariff.

Phil Gilbert, director of net zero delivery at E.ON Next, says the figures reflect a growing desire among households to “take control of their bills and rely less on the grid.”

“More and more households are realising just how much they can save by generating and storing their own energy,” he summarises.

Could 2026 set another solar record?

With more than 142,000 installations already completed during the first half of the year, 2026 could surpass 2025’s record if demand remains strong.

Whether solar panels make financial sense for an individual household will still depend on factors including the property's roof, the size and cost of the system and how much of the electricity generated can be used at home.

But after a record 2025 and the strongest start to a year in 15 years, the latest figures suggest rooftop solar is becoming an increasingly common feature of UK homes.

Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to stay afloat as Fifa president after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.

The Republic of Ireland have become the latest to officially pull their support for Infantino, joining England, Wales and other European nations have led the charge in withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027, while Uefa asserted that its boycott of Fifa competitions still stands in a bid to oust him from power.

The global players union, Fifpro, have also turned on Infantino, accusing him of a “profound abuse of presidential power” in an explosive statement.

However, Infantino’s allies are beginning to surface, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf, the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president.

As dominoes continue to fall, here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino:

Who has withdrawn its support for Infantino?

Uefa 🇪🇺

Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership, insisting that its boycott of Fifa competitions still stands despite the sell-off scheme being scrapped.

It points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.

The French Football Federation, however, have indicated to BBC Sport that they still intend to compete at next month’s U20 Women’s World Cup despite the confederation-wide boycott.

England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿

The English FA are one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027.

Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme.

open image in gallery FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino ( PA )

Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

The Football Association of Wales were one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino.

“The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Republic of Ireland 🇮🇪

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance.

"Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.”

Finland 🇫🇮

Finland kickstarted this process, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino.

Serbia 🇷🇸

The Football Association of Serbia then sent a similar letter to Fifa.

“We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read.

Sweden 🇸🇪

Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election.

"This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists."

open image in gallery Infantino has officially lost the endorsement of numerous Uefa nations ( PA )

Croatia 🇭🇷

As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president.

"This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time."

Albania 🇦🇱

The Albanian Football Federation also took the same stance, aligning with Uefa.

“The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed.

Greece 🇬🇷

The Greek federation similarly sent their withdrawal of support Fifa’s way.

Who is also opposing Infantino?

Concacaf (Confederation for North America and the Caribbean) 🌎

Concacaf have come out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject.

After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.”

It also wrote a joint statement with Uefa and the AFC which intended to give Infantino the opportunity to resign with dignity.

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is widely being seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election.

open image in gallery Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is widely being seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino ( Getty )

AFC (Asian Football Confederation) 🌏

The AFC was similarly aggrieved by the non-existent consultation from Fifa regarding the Infantino’s scheme, rejecting the proposal before calling on Fifa to undertake an “urgent review of its governance”.

The confederation’s part in a joint statement with Uefa and Concacaf confirms their desire to see Infantino ousted from power.

Germany 🇩🇪

The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance.

“The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board."

Denmark 🇩🇰

Denmark are in a similar position to Germany, having not endorsed Infantino’s re-election bid prior to the scheme’s reveal.

There is also a precedent for their opposition to Infantino, with federation president Jesper Moller not supporting his re-election efforts back in 2022: “There is only one candidate ... but Denmark will not be supporting the current president.”

Norway 🇳🇴

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) have been one of the most vocal bodies to call for Infantino’s resignation, and while they have not yet officially sent a letter to withdraw their support in him, such action is expected in the coming days.

NFF president Lise Klaveness told the Guardian: “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now. We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

open image in gallery Lise Klaveness has called on Infantino to resign ( Reuters )

Netherlands 🇳🇱

The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is also yet to officially withdraw its support but is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read.

Romania 🇷🇴

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) were among the countries to resolutely reject the sell-off proposal, calling it “a dangerous initiative to turn football into a private asset.

As a result, the FRF will withold support for Infantino’s re-election for the time being, with a statement reading: “FRF is suspending the discussion regarding the support of Fifa President Gianni Infantino for a new term, until further clarifications.”

Northern Ireland ☘️

The Northern Irish football association (IFA) has expressed “concerns” over Infantino’s leadership but has not officially withdrawn its support yet, unlike neighbours Ireland.

"We take our responsibilities as a member association of both Uefa and Fifa seriously," said an IFA spokesperson. "We support the current Uefa position on the matter and will continue to engage constructively on issues relating to football governance. We are of course aware of the recent developments and wider concerns within the football community. We are considering these matters carefully and will continue to engage through the appropriate governance structures and channels.”

Jordan 🇯🇴

Jordan are so far the only non-Uefa member association to publicly oppose Infantino after federation president Prince Ali bin Hussein levelled accusations of blackmail against Fifa.

Prince Ali alleged the organisation offered assistance with the kingdom's issues in exchange for his endorsement, following Infantino's withdrawal from a World Cup stake sale proposal. Among the problems cited was the association's eight-month wait for prize money, due since December for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

After taking to X to reveal the outstanding payments, the Jordan Football Association received the prize money two days later - but Prince Ali has not changed his stance over not endorsing Infantino: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

Sierra Leone 🇸🇱

Former Sierra Leone FA president and ex-Fifa Council member Isha Johansen has indicated that Africa’s support of Infantino is not unanimous across the continent after emerging as one of the African voices opposing the privatisation project.

He urged African football chiefs to think carefully about the game’s future, saying: "What price does one have to pay in order to get to this elevated development for football in Africa?"

Canada 🇨🇦

Canada prime minister Mark Carney joined his UK counterpart Andy Burnham in calling for Infantino to be ousted from his position as president.

“It should be fatal,” Carney said, whose country co-hosted this summer’s World Cup. “Certainly I don’t have confidence in Mr Infantino."

However, the country has confirmed it will not boycott Fifa competitions and participate in the U20 Women’s World Cup in Poland.

Guyana 🇬🇾

The Guyanese Football Federation, a South American nation under Concacaf but surrounded by Conmebol’s Infantino allies, has “fully endorsed” Concacaf’s statement condemning Infantino’s leadership.

“Good governance, transparency, accountability and institutional integrity remain fundamental principles that guide the work of the Guyanese Football Federation,” a statement read.

Recommended The Curacao blueprint and how Guyana are targeting a similar World Cup miracle

Who is supporting Infantino?

Caf (African Football Confederation) 🌍

Caf, the governing body for African football, has become the first confederation to unanimously back Infantino. Its 54 member associations account more than a quarter of Fifa’s 211 members.

“We are committed to continue working together with Fifa, its member associations, other football confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of football worldwide,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said.

Motsepe later added thar the position of embattled president Infantino can only be decided by Fifa elections.

Argentina 🇦🇷

Argentina became the first member from South America to voice its support for Infantino, on the same day that confederation Conmebol - which had thus far only expressed support of Infantino - expressed concern over Fifa’s procedures.

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the Fifa board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Argentina president Javier Milei (left) behind Infantino at the "Board of Peace" hosted by US president Donald Trump ( AFP/Getty )

Mexico 🇲🇽

Mexico joined Argentina from the Americas, breaking rank from the United States, Canada and the rest of Concacaf that had condemned Infantino’s plan and aligned itself against his leadership.

The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) stated: "The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made... by President Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations."

Paraguay 🇵🇾

Paraguay has also followed suit as Infantino’s Conmebol support base begins to surface.

Their federation published a letter of support addressed to Infantino, writing that it "reaffirms its commitment to continue working alongside Fifa”.

Qatar 🇶🇦

Qatar was the first football association to publicly back Infantino, even though they later welcomed the decision to scrap the plan.

"While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among member associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Qatar's FA has backed Infantino to continue as president ( Getty Images )

Sri Lanka 🇱🇰

Like Qatar, Sri Lanka welcomed the decision to scrap the investment plan and has since reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

"One of President Infantino's defining leadership qualities has always been his willingness to listen to the views and concerns of Member Associations. This decision is a clear reflection of his inclusive leadership style, built on dialogue, mutual respect, and a genuine commitment to serving the global football community," its statement read.

Kuwait 🇰🇼

Like others, Kuwait welcomed the decision to halt the plans but Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Al-Sabah, the president of the Kuwait Football Association, affirmed his support for Infantino.

A statement read: “He concluded by affirming the Kuwait Football Association's confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino, and its support for efforts aimed at developing the game and enhancing its opportunities for growth in a way that serves all national associations and achieves the shared interests of global football.”

Lebanon 🇱🇧

Lebanon, who granted Infantino citizenship last year, have backed the Swiss-Italian, with FA president Hashim Haidar all but echoing the same sentiments as Kuwait.

“Haidar reaffirms the Lebanese Football Association’s support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and his confidence in the decisions he makes in the best interests of global football, as well as in his efforts and initiatives aimed at developing the game,” he said, while also asserting that Infantino’s proposal “could be re-examined ... in a away that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity”.

Indonesia 🇮🇩

The president of the Indonesian FA supported Infantino’s sell-off plan and has now backed him for another term.

Hailing Fifa as a “strategic partner that is truly present” in its football development, Erick Thohir said: “This is proof of President Infantino’s vision that football development must not be centered on a single region; it must proceed worldwide.”

Philippines 🇵🇭

Philippines have also backed Infantino and backed for co-operation among confederations.

"We stand behind President Gianni Infantino's leadership, and trust that continued dialogue among all confederations and member associations will keep the global game moving forward together,” the Philippines confirmed.

Mongolia 🇲🇳

Joining the Philippines, the Mongolian Football Federation has put out a statement in support of Infantino.

Bhutan 🇧🇹

The Bhutan Football Federation has published a letter that extends its “sincere appreciation” to Infantino for scrapping the plans, hailing him for demonstrating “true leadership” by “prioritising consensus over commerce”.

“We stand united with Fifa and President Infantino in their ongoing efforts to serve the global football community,” wrote federation president Dasho Ugen Tsechup.

Morocco 🇲🇦

The location of Infantino’s crisis meeting on Wednesday, Morocco have stuck by the Swiss-Italian as one of his most loyal allies.

“What has been achieved in recent years through Fifa’s development programmes, particularly in Africa, represents an important accomplishment that must be preserved, to the benefit of all member associations,” said the Royal Moroccan Football Federation’s president Fouzi Lekjaa.

open image in gallery Infantino held his crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco ( AP )

Egypt 🇪🇬

Similar to their north African counterpart, Egypt have maintained their endorsement of Infantino.

"The Egyptian Football Association reiterates its full trust in President Gianni Infantino's leadership and its continuous support for any initiatives that benefit Fifa member associations and the future of world football,” a statement read.

Mauritania 🇲🇷

Ahmed Yahya, the country's representative on the Fifa Council, was one of a number of African football leaders to say he was backing Infantino early on, pledging his support before Caf took its stance.

Niger 🇳🇪

Same as above, with Hamidou Djibrilla from Niger coming out quickly in support of Infantino.

Sudan 🇸🇩

Sudan’s federation joined five other Arab nations - Qatar, Lebanon, Morocco, Egypt and Mauritania - in writing a joint statement backing Infantino.

"Recognising the important role of Arab football in bringing people together and strengthening co-operation among football associations across the Arab world, we ... express our full support for Mr Gianni Infantino, president of Fifa, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," the statement read.

"We deeply appreciate Mr Infantino’s sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game’s role in bringing people and communities together. We look forward to continuing our close cooperation with him towards a stronger and more prosperous future for world ‌football, expanding opportunities and further enhancing Arab football’s contribution to ​the global game."

DR Congo 🇨🇩

DR Congo's federation (Fecofa) president Veron Mosengo-Omba, who was only elected in May, spoke out in “full support”. of Infantino. The two studied at university in Switzerland together.

Fecofa said it had "greatly benefited" from Fifa's programmes, citing investment in development and infrastructure.

Nigeria 🇳🇬

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has largely aligned itself towards a supportive stance for Infantino's leadership, with former NFF president and deputy chairman of Fifa's Men's National Teams Competitions Committee, Amaju Pinnick, backing his initial sell-off plan.

Comoros 🇰🇲

The president of the Comoros Football Federation, Said Ali Athouman, also backed Infantino’s scheme due to the financial benefits to smaller nations.

"Our problem is how to obtain money,” he said. “Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete? The richest nations can train players, have infrastructure and equipment, and it's no coincidence that they then achieve results. Most European countries don't have ​these problems.”

open image in gallery A number of African nations have fallen in line with the stance of Caf president Patrice Motsepe ( Getty )

Malawi 🇲🇼

Fleetwood Haiya, Malawi's football chief, echoed the same concerns in his support for Infantino.

He told BBC Sport: "Our government is not able to make sure that they have medical supplies in hospitals and at the same time to look at football. Malawi needs money."

Uganda 🇺🇬

The Ugandan federation are said to have echoed Malawi’s sentiments, with football officials from the federation telling BBC Sport that Fifa investment has transformed their game both on and off the pitch.

Gambia 🇬🇲

Lamin Kaba Bajo told BBC Sport that his federation not just stood by Infantino, but would do "everything within our means" to get him re-elected.

"That's my personal opinion as president of the federation, and a good number of African memberships also stand on that line. He is here to stay,” he said.

Djibouti 🇩🇯

The Djiboutian Football Federation has similarly welcomed the decision to withdraw the sell-off proposal, with president Souleiman Hassan Waberi saying the climbdown “demonstrates a firm commitment to preserving the unity, solidarity and cohesion that define the football family”.

He said in a statement: “I reaffirm my full support for Fifa President Mr Gianni Infantino and for all initiatives aimed at promoting the sustainable, transparent and inclusive development of football around the world.”

South Africa 🇿🇦

While not an official statement from the federation, South Africa’s Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of South Africa, Gayton McKenzie, posted on X saying that Infantino had been "very good to African football".

"Africa should be cautious in joining the public lynching of Infantino,” he warned. “He has been very good to African football. We can debate his ideas but let's not forget who has been a friend to us. Many of those calling for his head want the old status quo back too."

Who are yet to confirm a stance?

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has not publicly stated its position, though its biggest footballing nation New Zealand did come out in opposition to Infantino’s proposal. New Zealand have, however, vowed to play at the U20 Women’s World Cup.

Conmebol, the governing body for South America, also took a while to break its silence. It expressed “concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken” and welcomed the decision to withdraw the plans, affirming it will “not support any action” that “ignores or deviates” from the “democratic procedures that represent the 211 Fifa member associations”. However, it is believed the confederation will continue to back Infantino having previously been very supportive of the incumbent president, with Conmebol pushing for a 64-team World Cup for the 2030 edition.

News.title: Transfer news LIVE: Chelsea set Enzo Fernandez deadline, Barcola to Liverpool latest, Konsa to Arsenal
News.content:
Chelsea have told Manchester City that they have until Friday to submit a bid for midfielder Enzo Fernandez. The Blues have informed their Premier League rivals that they will need to sepnd £120m to sign the World Cup runner-up. City, meanwhile, remain in talks with Barcelona over Rodri, who is available for £60m, and are also interested in the signing of World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. Winger Savinho is moving closer to leaving the Etihad for Tottenham in a £65m deal though.

Mikel Arteta has said that Arsenal’s business is not done yet, with the Gunners receiving interest in Gabriel Martinelli from Galatasaray as well as Chelsea and Manchester United reportedly turning down the chance to sign Myles Lewis-Skelly. Arsenal have set their sights high and are interested in adding a marquee signing: they will have to play the long game in moves for Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez and Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola.

Barcola also leads Liverpool’s list of transfer targets and the Reds are in talks with PSG over a fee, though the European champions are demanding £145m to sell the winger. PSG chairman Nasser Al-Khelaifi did not rule out a move for Barcola, however, saying: “We’re working calmly, we don’t talk too much. I can’t say whether he will leave or not. Today, he is a PSG player. We’ll see.”

News.content:

Temperatures are expected to soar to 37C in parts of England on Thursday as a fresh heatwave sweeps across the country bringing drought, wildfires and urgent health warnings.

Following persistent hot and dry weather this week, swathes of southern England can expect weather warmer than in the sunny Greek capital of Athens, which is forecast to see highs of 33C.

Temperature highs will peak across Oxfordshire and the Chilterns on Thursday afternoon before cloudy weather brings some relief on Friday. An amber extreme heat warning has been issued, covering part of London.

Almost three-quarters of England is now suffering from drought conditions, affecting 45 million people, with the country now on course to record its hottest ever summer.

open image in gallery The Met Office forecasts highs of 34C in the capital around 4pm. But in some parts outside the capital, temperatures could swell to 37C, they say ( Met Office )

The prime minister has now urged retailers to stop selling disposable barbecues while the dry conditions endure in a desperate bid to curb the risk of wildfires breaking out.

His comments came after chairing a meeting of the Government’s emergency Cobra committee in response to the prolonged spell of exceptionally hot and dry weather.

England and Wales have already seen as many wildfires this year as in the whole of 2025.

The Met Office’s deputy chief forecaster Mike Silverstone said the heatwave was expected to be fairly widespread across England and Wales.

open image in gallery London and Oxford can expect the worst of the weather on Thursday ( Met Office )

“A fairly widespread heatwave is likely across large parts of England and Wales, with hot conditions developing in places,” he said.

“Humidity levels are also expected to increase through the week, which may make conditions feel more uncomfortable, particularly overnight.”

The UK has experienced a consistent North-South split in the weather across this summer, with Scotland and Northern Ireland experiencing heavy spells of rain last weekend.

Rare amber “extreme heat” warnings have been issued by the Met Office for London and parts of the South East, East Midlands, East of England, West Midlands and South Yorkshire from 9am to midnight on Thursday.

The Met Office’s latest forecast for Oxford read: “Temperatures rising quickly under strong sunshine. Feeling hot or locally very hot. As a result, an amber extreme heat warning has been issued, and this covers part of London. Maximum temperature 37 °C.”

open image in gallery All of England is under a heat health alert ( UKHSA/gov.uk )

All of England is under an amber heat health alert lasting until 9pm on Friday.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) warned of risks to the lives of the elderly and vulnerable people and significant effects on health and social care services.

Train passengers are also being urged to only travel if necessary by some operators on Thursday as services will be disrupted because of hot weather.

open image in gallery The Chilterns and parts of Oxfordshire will bear the brunt of the heat on Thursday ( Met Office )

Chiltern Railways and East Midlands Railway issued alerts to “only travel if essential”.

Other operators will either run a reduced timetable or are warning about the potential for short-notice cancellations.

Southern Water has meanwhile applied for a rare drought order which would ban businesses from non-essential water use, including cleaning cars and filling non-domestic swimming pools, saying an “exceptional” lack of rain has threatened supplies in Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

It warned that 165,000 people in the Southampton West supply area could face restricted supplies.

Met Office five-day weather forecast

Tonight

London and the south east can expect more dry conditions overnight from Wednesday with prolonged clear periods and variable cloud. The Met Office forecasts minumum temperatures of 16C.

Thursday

Very warm becoming hot or very hot across much of England and Wales. Chance of an isolated evening shower in the northeast. Heavier showers for Northern Ireland and Scotland later.

Temperatures quickly rising in the morning in the north west. Some cloud developing by afternoon, with maximum temperatures of 33C. Highs of 37C possible in Banbury, Oxfordshire.

Friday

Mixed conditions, with sunny spells in the south. More cloud, showers and occasional rain in the north. Temperatures near normal, but warm in the southeast.

Cloudier and fresher conditions can be expected in London and the northwest.

Saturday

A continuation from Friday into Saturday with some odd showers expected nationwide.

Sunday

Dry with sunny spells on Sunday, before clouding over from the west late afternoon. A spell of more organised rain could arrive in the north west later in the day as winds strengthen.

Dry with sunny spells in the middle of the country on Sunday, before clouding over through the afternoon.

Keely Hodgkinson eased to victory in her 800m semi-final at the European Athletics Championships to remain on course for another major international medal, but there was a shock in the previous semi-final as hot favourite Audrey Werro was clipped and fell.

Hodgkinson won her semi-final in 1:57.38 from Femke Broeders-Bol, who looked comfortable on her shoulder in an unfamiliar event for the Dutchwoman, having stepped up from her usual 400m hurdles this year.

Werro, the fastest woman in the world this year, led the first semi-final from the start and responded to accelerations from Britain’s Jemma Reekie and French record holder Anais Bourgoin.

But the 22-year-old appeared to be clipped from behind on the final bend and hit the deck hard, with Lithuania’s Gabija Galvydyte also falling as the other runners attempted to evade the fallen Swiss.

Werro eventually got to her feet and finished the race, crossing the line last looking heavily winded and clutching her ribs. Referees advanced both her and Galvydyte to the final after appeals, meaning 10 athletes will race for the title on Friday.

Werro told the BBC afterwards: “I was feeling really great until the last metre, unfortunately, I don’t know, something happened and I was on the ground. I hope I will be qualified for the final.”

She confirmed that she kept running in order to be able to appeal for a place in the final, if video replays suggested she was hindered by another athlete: “This is the reason why I finished the race and it’s always important to go until the end, now we will see what happened.”

Reekie came through to win the semi-final in 1:58.61, with Bourgoin and Switzerland’s Veronica Vancardo completing the trio of automatic qualifiers.

Werro ran the fastest time in four decades earlier this season, with her new personal best of 1:53.80 the third-fastest of all time, making her the favourite to take gold in Birmingham’s Alexander Stadium and setting up a blockbuster clash with Olympic champion Hodgkinson and Broeders-Bol.

In the second semi-final Hodgkinson hit the front early with Broeders-Bol latching onto her shoulder, with the pair pulling away in the home straight. Italy’s Eloisa Coiro, who set a new national record in the first round, was the last of the automatic qualifiers.

open image in gallery Werro fell hard in the first semi-final ( PA )

open image in gallery She was able to finish the race but appeared badly winded ( Reuters )

Hodgkinson was asked by BBC Sport whether she had seen Werro’s fall. She said: “I heard a ‘oohhh’ [from the crowd] which is never a good sign; I don’t know what it looked like,” she said. “You can’t worry about what other people are doing [in your race]. It’s a real shame, I hope she’s okay and that she’s in the final tomorrow.

“The depth was really good, another 1:57, overall happy, can’t complain. The excitement [for the women’s 800m] makes me excited, I love a good challenge, it brings out the best in me.

“I hope for a clean race with no falling over. And no wind please, I'm going to talk to an Esty witch to make sure there's no wind,” she smiled.

Broeders-Bol meanwhile said seeing Werro fall had made her feel “extra cautious” in her semi. She said her plan had been to lead “from the front, either with Keely or in front of Keely, I think it worked out perfectly.

“I saw it [the fall], I didn’t watch a replay because it often looks terrible. I hope she’s okay. It made me extra cautious.”

Europe is in the grip of its fifth heatwave this summer, raising fears that extreme temperatures could trigger another set of wildfires across the continent.

Wildfires have scorched more than 505,000 hectares (ha) of land across Europe during an unusually active wildfire season. A relatively wet winter that fuelled growth in vegetation was followed by rolling heatwaves, which dried it all out, making the land more prone to catching fire.

During the same period, the extreme heat has been linked to 25,000 deaths this year, according to Bloomberg research covering Spain, France, the UK, the Netherlands and Switzerland.

Western Europe is suffering its hottest ever summer, with temperatures well above average.

On Thursday, temperatures are set to reach highs of 42C in Spain, including in the popular tourist hotspot of Cordoba, and 39C in Bordeaux, where a huge blaze forced the evacuation of more than 200,000 people last month.

Here, The Independent looks at where the risk of wildfires will be in the coming days.

Fire danger forecast

open image in gallery Large swathes of the continent remain under ‘very high’ wildfire risk, with some patches (shown in dark red) at ‘extreme’ risk ( Copernicus EFFIS )

The EFFIS current situation viewer shows vast swathes of western, central, eastern and southeastern Europe are at “very high” risk of a wildfire on Thursday. Some areas, shown in dark red on the map, are at “extreme” risk.

The main wildfire threat will continue moving eastwards before abating in much of western Europe early next week, when southern Spain and central European countries are at the highest risk.

Fires were ongoing in western Europe as of Thursday with around 1,200 people evacuated from a campsite on Wednesday after two wildfires spread near a beach in the country’s north.

The prefecture for the administrative department of Pas-de-Calais, in the country's north and bordering the Strait of Dover, said one of the wildfires was under control, but conditions were "unfavourable" for the other one. Access was difficult and the fire was spreading unimpeded toward the south.

Entire regions burnt

open image in gallery Record amounts of land have burnt in the EU in 2026 ( Copernicus EFFIS )

A record amount of land has burnt this summer, surpassing the total for 2025 at this time of the year and more than double the 20-year average between 2006 and 2025.

As of 5 August, some 505,583 hectares (ha) of land had burnt, compared to 379,392 at this point in 2025, and well above the 2006 to 2025 average of 197,347 ha.

The fires have already cost the continent up to £16.4 billion in economic costs, estimates published by forecaster AccuWeather showed last Thursday. This includes the cost of emergency response, damage to property, and health impacts.

In one of the largest fires around Bordeaux, a record-setting fire burned around 420 square kilometres of land.

Record-breaking temperatures

open image in gallery The continent is far warmer than average for this time of year ( Copernicus EFFIS )

Western Europe reported a record-breaking 24-hour average temperature of 21.62C for June and July, according to a report by the EU’s Copernicus climate change service released on Monday.

This is 2.79C above the average temperature during the 1991 to 2020 period, smashing the previous heat record set in 2022.

Spanish forecaster Aemet says that tourist hotspots in Spain including Cordoba (42C), Sevilla (40C), Granada (39C), and Madrid (39C) will all see temperatures in the region of 40C on Thursday, while other touristy areas including Barcelona, Malaga and Alicante are all forecast to be in the low-to-mid 30s in the coming days.

Large parts of Spain, barring the eastern, southern and northwestern coasts, will be placed under yellow and amber warnings for the next three days.

In France, temperatures will near 40C in the popular tourist spots of Bordeaux, Nantes, and Toulouse.

Average rainfall plummets

open image in gallery Europe's summer has also been unusually dry, with red areas on the map showing areas with below average rainfall ( Copernicus EFFIS )

Prolonged drought conditions have played a critical role in driving up the wildfire risk, with droughts that began in May deteriorating in July and August.

Data from the European Drought Observatory updated on 10 August shows that 50 per cent of the UK and EU is suffering some level of drought intensity, whether at “watch”, “warning” or “alert” level. Nine per cent was at the alert level in July.

Almost the entire continent, barring parts of Scandinavia, is set to experience less rainfall than usual in the week between 10 and 16 August, according to estimations by Copernicus based on the ECMWF Monthly Forecast System.

Europe’s four major rivers, the Loire, Po, Rhune and Danube, have been pushed to record low levels this month, according to Copernicus.

“The drought has built up since early spring due to lower rainfall and higher than average temperatures, turning into fuel for the devastating wildfires in France and Spain in July,” the EU’s Joint Research Centre said.
