Sports.title: Revealed: What Diego Simeone told Julian Alvarez in showdown talks after Arsenal target reiterated his desire to leave Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez has spoken to Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone for the first time since declaring that he wants to leave the club in order to 'fulfil my dream'.

The highly coveted Argentina forward, 26, is being tracked by several of Europe's biggest clubs, including Premier League champions Arsenal, LaLiga champions Barcelona and Real Madrid.

While representing Argentina at this summer's World Cup, Alvarez publicly declared his desire to leave Atletico, saying: 'I try to be an honest person. I spoke with the people at Atletico Madrid, and I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfill my dream.'

Although reports have suggested Barcelona are Alvarez's preferred destination, Atletico have remained steadfast in their position that he is not for sale. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said last month that the club would not entertain any offers for the striker, even in the region of £170m (€200 million).

Alvarez has a £428m (€500m) release clause and Atletico have already rejected a £129m (€150m) bid from Real Madrid.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week and, ahead of Wednesday's session, reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex.

The striker returned to pre-season training this week after publicly declaring he would like to leave the club this summer in order to 'fulfil my dream'

Alvarez reportedly spent around 10 minutes speaking with Simeone (above) at Atletico's Cerro del Espino training complex, and reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation

According to reports, Alvarez, who is nicknamed La Arana, or 'The Spider', because of his Spider-Man celebration, reiterated his desire to leave during the conversation.

In response, Simeone is said to have restated the position he outlined publicly last week, namely that Atletico are planning for Alvarez to remain at the club.

'The situation is very clear, the club made a decision that Miguel Angel explained very well,' Simeone said. 'We are very happy with Julian. From a sporting perspective, we will help him to continue growing, to continue improving, and to give us back what he has given us in these two years, which was a great deal.'

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024. He recorded 20 goals and nine assists in all competitions last season, while his 10 Champions League goals left him behind only Mbappe and Harry Kane in the scoring charts.

Back in April, Simeone said: 'I am not in Julian Alvarez's head. I suppose it is normal that an extraordinary player like Julian is wanted by Arsenal, Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona. It's normal because he's very good.'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has admitted there are 'very few players' in world football capable of immediately improving his starting XI, but insists the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer.

Arsenal were heavily linked with Vinicius Jr before he signed a new contract with Real Madrid. They have, however, already secured the signing of Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes for £75m.

The former Manchester City player, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, joined Atletico in an £81.5m deal in 2024

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, meanwhile, has insisted that the Gunners are still trying to make another marquee signing this summer

'I think for the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring that to the club,' Arteta said after Arsenal's 1-1 draw with Como on Wednesday.

'Every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth to the squad, we need to do that,' he said. 'We are actively trying to do so. The thing in the market is that it doesn't just depend on you. We are very clear on that.'

With more than two weeks remaining in the transfer window, there is still plenty of time for the situation to develop, while Arsenal may also benefit from Atletico's strained relationship with their LaLiga rivals.

One example came in June after Atletico rejected Real Madrid's £129m offer for Alvarez.

Real released a statement saying: 'Following the meeting of the board of directors held today, it has made an offer of 150 million euros to Club Atletico de Madrid for the federative rights of the player Julian Alvarez.

'After reviewing and evaluating the offer, Club Atletico de Madrid has expressed its gratitude for the proposal, made within the framework of the good relations between both clubs, and has rejected it, referring to the player's release clause.'

Atletico quoted the statement on X alongside a series of laughing emojis.

In a follow-up post, they added: 'You must have confused education with gratitude, but to leave no doubt: we don't thank you for anything.

'We neither study nor consider any offer for Julian. How could we not get along, when you make us laugh even more than Barcelona does.'

In a final swipe, Atletico posted: 'P.S. Taking advantage of the good relationship with your new president, let's see if you stop 'stealing' players from our Academy. Thanks a lot, @realmadrid!'

Sports.title: 'Hopefully I'm on a plane to Vegas and I've scored 507 goals!': Josh Windass on Wrexham's Premier League dream, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac - and the 'magic spell' behind Phil Parkinson's incredible tenure
Sports.content:
Josh Windass is not your stereotypical footballer.

Refreshingly honest, the forward, son of cult hero Dean, doesn’t celebrate when he scores – insisting ‘I just don’t get happy’ – and admitted his American in-laws knew more about Wrexham than him when he joined the club last summer.

For most players, a calf injury that meant they were unable to play a part in Wrexham’s pre-season tour of the US would have been enough to get them down.

But not Windass.

‘We’ve been on tour in America,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘So it’s just been brilliant for me. I’ve been on holiday for two weeks, doing my rehab in the sun!

‘It is frustrating not to be playing but I’m not one for pre-season games. I think they’re all nonsense. Whether you win or lose, the proof will be in the pudding.’

Wrexham No 10 Josh Windass is hoping to lead Phil Parkinson's side to the Premier League

Windass scored 16 goals and provided five assists in just 28 league starts last season

Windass’ dry humour shines through during our conversation and despite his setback, he hopes to be fit for Wrexham’s Championship opener against Cardiff – if not their second game with Watford.

It would be a shame for him to have to wait much longer after he enjoyed one of the best seasons of his career last term.

Having departed Sheffield Wednesday on the eve of the campaign amid their financial turmoil, Windass scored 16 goals and provided five assists in just 28 league starts.

The No 10 was one of 13 summer arrivals as Wrexham endured an inevitable adaptation period following three successive promotions.

But, over the winter, Phil Parkinson's side climbed the table and ultimately missed out on the play-offs in heartbreaking fashion on the final day after drawing with Middlesbrough.

‘I was disappointed we didn’t make the play-offs as that was our aim,’ Windass says. ‘But I try and do as best as I can and, as a No 10, you want to score and set up goals.

‘From Christmas onwards we were one of the top three or four teams in the league and, once you've got the proof you can do it (it’s massive). If we'd have done that all season, we'd have had a good chance of promotion.'

Windass has played for some big clubs in his career, including Rangers, but insists nothing compares to what he has experienced at Wrexham over the past 12 months.

'It is the best culture I've ever been in by a country mile,' says Windass of Wrexham's dressing room

‘I don't know how he (Phil Parkinson) does it, because every club I've been at, you always have a few people you sign who are not great (personalities)'

‘It's honestly incredible,’ he adds. ‘Before you get there, everyone says, “Oh, it's the best dressing room ever, the culture's amazing”. And you're like, yeah, sure it is.

‘But it is the best dressing room and culture I've ever been in by a country mile. What the gaffer, Ryan (Reynolds) and Rob (Mac) have created with everybody, how they get on with each other – in football you generally don't get that in changing rooms. Here it's different.'

Parkinson doesn’t get the credit he deserves for what has been a transformative five-year spell in North Wales.

He is now the fourth longest-serving manager in English football and, despite significant turnover in the playing squad, he has remained throughout Wrexham’s evolution from a struggling non-League side into one of the most marketable clubs in the world.

So, what's the secret?

‘He's had so much success,’ Windass says. ‘The way he recruits players for the dressing room, not just for the style of play (is amazing).

‘I don't think he's made a bad signing in terms of that. He does his due diligence with character references. He signs good players, but ultimately he signs boys who want to fight for each other and get on, both on and off the pitch.

‘I don't know how he does it, because every club I've been at, you always have a few people you sign who are not great for the dressing room.

‘But at Wrexham it's like he's got a magic spell because everyone comes in and is top class.’

On Wrexham's Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, Windass adds: 'They’re the same with every player. They speak to us all the time and we're just a reflection of them. They're winners and the club has shown that in the last five years.’

Windass is full of praise for Wrexham's Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds (left) and Rob Mac

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson is expected to boost Wrexham's promotion bid

As Wrexham have risen through the leagues, each summer has been accompanied by significant change in the squad.

Yet, with Parkinson’s side set to play a second campaign in the same division for the first time since their promotion from the National League, this has been one of continuity.

Crystal Palace full back Danny Imray, who shone on loan at West Brom last season, and Preston captain Ben Whiteman are the only players through the door, although more arrivals are expected – including Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson. Steve Nickson also joined from Newcastle as director of football.

And Windass believes a more settled squad could prove to be a significant benefit to Wrexham, although he admits they must improve defensively after they shipped more goals than relegated Oxford last season.

‘That’s the nail on the head,’ he adds. ‘I don't think people realise how many new players we had on the pitch last year, and maybe that's why it took until Christmas for us to gel and start playing well.

‘We've got 98 per cent of the team still here, we're all used to playing with each other and we get on great. The new signings have settled in seamlessly, so we're going to have a good chance.’

As our conversation comes to a close, Windass’ wit is on display again when asked what a dream campaign would look like if we were talking again at the end of the season.

‘Hopefully, I'm on a plane to Vegas having just won promotion,’ he says. 'And I've scored 20… no, I’ve scored 507 goals!’

Sports.title: Premier League pre-season friendly descends into chaos with a penalty taken against an OPEN GOAL after Fulham walked off in row over new manager Alvaro Arbeloa's red card
Sports.content:
Premier League pre-season friendly descends into chaos with a penalty taken against an OPEN GOAL after Fulham walked off in row over new manager Alvaro Arbeloa's red card

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Fulham's friendly with Malaga on Wednesday night was that in name only after an acrimonious ending after the full-time whistle, which included new manager Alvaro Arbeloa being sent off.

The Cottagers drew 2-2 at their Spanish opponents - with the hosts claiming a draw courtesy of Eneko Jauregi's 90th-minute penalty after Calvin Bassey was penalised for a handball.

However, that's where the drama started...

With the match ending in a draw, Malaga's players were preparing for a penalty shootout to determine who would win the Costa del Sol Trophy.

But there was one sticking point... Fulham's players were not and instead headed down the tunnel, sparking boos from the home supporters.

It led to some confusion on the pitch as Eneko picked up the ball and rolled a penalty into an empty net to ironic celebrations from him and his team-mates and the majority of the 17,179 fans inside La Rosaleda.

🎬⚽️ Absolute cinema! During a pre-season friendly between Malaga and Fulham that ended in a 2-2 draw, the La Liga club was ready to do a penalty shootout, but Fulham left the field saying a shootout wasn’t in the friendly contract.



So a Malaga player took one in the empty net… pic.twitter.com/mF2qX5eHVx — Ultras Clips (@ultras_clips) August 12, 2026

Fulham's players refused to take part in a penalty shootout after drawing 2-2 at Malaga

In a bizarre ending to the match, Malaga ended up winning the Costa del Sol Trophy

Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa was sent off after full-time as he was unhappy with the referee

After the match Fulham released a statement explaining why they didn't partake in the shootout, writing on X: 'Thank you for your excellent support in Malaga this evening!

'We can confirm that prior to the match, both teams agreed that there would not be a penalty shootout in the event of a draw.'

According to beIN Sports, Fulham also didn't get involved in a shootout as it could affect their travel plans.

If that incident wasn't enough there was also the small matter of Arbeloa's dismissal who was unhappy with the referee at full-time.

As official Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias blew for the end of the game, Arbeloa made a beeline for him before being shown a red card.

Spanish outlet Marca was damning of Arbeloa and Fulham's actions, writing: 'This was a deplorable act of disrespect and an unprecedented lack of respect in the history of the Malaga friendly.

'During the break to decide who would take the penalties, Arbeloa clashed with referee Ortiz Arias and was shown a straight red card.

'Amid the ensuing chaos, Fulham decided to leave the field and refuse to participate in the penalty shootout, in one of the most embarrassing incidents in the history of football in Malaga.'

Sports.title: Man United star flies in personal stylist from the Netherlands just to clear out clothes he doesn't wear
Sports.content:
Man United star Joshua Zirkzee flew in a personal stylist from his homeland to help him clear his wardrobe.

The Dutch forward, 25, used the services of fashion expert Sydney Luchies to sort out his clothes and reorganise his closet.

In a recent post to her TikTok account, Luchies documented her day in Manchester, where she flew in to from the Netherlands before jetting straight back after her work was done.

In the video, she said: 'Come with me to do a closet clean for Joshua Zirkzee. Joshua asked if I could help him reorganise his closet, create a bit more space for new things, and make it all neat and organised.'

In the clip, Luchies proceeded to show herself sorting and tidying Zirkzee's clothes, with the 25-year-old having a whole array of eye-catching outfits.

She had to choose which items to get rid of and what to keep, and she made sure everything remained well-ordered in his sprawling walk-in wardrobe.

Joshua Zirkzee had a fashion stylist travels ✈️ to Manchester just to help reorganize his closet to create more space and make it neat organized. And fly back #mufc pic.twitter.com/GhxSXWm3WJ — Football clips (@Mohqoshin) August 4, 2026

Man United star Joshua Zirkzee flew in a personal stylist to help him clear out his wardrobe

Zirkzee used fashion expert Sydney Luchies, who he flew in from the Netherlands to help

Luchies has previously worked with Zirkzee when she helped him with his fashion style

The stylist later revealed that the items Zirkzee no longer needed would either be sold off in his name or packed up and given to charity.

In a previous TikTok, Luchies had given fans further insight into Zirkzee's life and his fashion style.

At the beginning of the clip, the stylist asked what sort of clothes the forward wanted before she built a mood board and created the outfits.

After Zirkzee's approval, she delivered them for a fitting, with the United star seen trying them all on.

'Come with me to do the personal styling for Joshua Zirkzee,' she said in the clip.

'Joshua lives in Manchester, so this time we flew to England.

'Once I arrived I started preparing for the fitting and Joshua wanted to look like a rapper from the 1990s with his own touch. I think we did well.'

Zirkzee has been at United for two years now, although he has struggled to earn a regular place in the team, scoring just five goals in 56 games.

He has impressed in pre-season though, and with United back in the Champions League this season there are likely to be more opportunities for him in 2026-27.

Sports.title: How Man City will replace Rodri - and the inconvenient truth for World Cup hero that shows they might be better off without him
Sports.content:
Rodri is due in Manchester on Friday, after his planned back surgery following World Cup glory meant he was given two extra days' holiday. But in the context of that rehabilitation and the harsh reality that his future now lies away from Manchester City, it wouldn’t represent a great surprise if the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner did not return to the building for regular pre-season testing.

City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for a central midfielder in the final year of his contract, who was awarded player of the tournament last month. Somebody who often looked physically shot last season, yet was imperious at international level.

There is a balance to strike for director of football Hugo Viana in making sure City maximise Rodri's value while also realising that this orchestrated exit – heavily signposted for a year and solidified by Pep Guardiola's goodbye, with the 30-year-old starting only 18 Premier League games in the last two seasons – likely only ends one way.

Guardiola called it last autumn, that City would not see the best of his metronome all season and that recaptured form would be reserved for the World Cup. The suggestion felt intriguing at the time, more by the way in which it was delivered – a little knowing, somewhat resigned. City’s medical staff were attempting to curb Rodri’s desire to rush various injury comebacks.

There are those who believe his performances Stateside, when temperatures dictated that games were played at a slower pace, prove that there is still nobody better across Europe than him. But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts.

In the Premier League, the win ratio is exactly half with him starting. Without, it is 60.3 per cent. A very similar story plays out from 29 starts in all competitions. Never before in Rodri’s City career have the team won more games in his absence.

Manchester City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for Rodri, who was awarded World Cup player of the tournament last month

But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts

Although not an exact science – City still always concede fewer goals when he’s the deep midfielder – and a small sample size, it does represent a comparison worthy of note.

City, and Enzo Maresca, would prefer to plough on with him, of course. Their movements in the transfer window paint a picture of how this is only heading one way.

Proactive and forceful club denials around interest in Chelsea’s £120million-rated Enzo Fernandez at the beginning of the summer have now given way to silence. Fernandez wants to reunite with his old boss Maresca and those close to him believe the feeling to be mutual. Ayyoub Bouaddi, the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million.

City sources say Bouaddi's arrival is not linked to Rodri’s future and that they are pursuing him regardless of what happens, in a window that is threatening to become busy if Tijjani Reijnders and potentially another midfielder leave.

Yet his displays across almost 100 senior games, earning rave reviews for a physicality off the ball and intelligence on it, dictate that he can be ready to impact City’s fortunes. His minutes will have to be carefully monitored and managed.

What seemed apparent on Wednesday, when Elliot Anderson was unveiled to supporters during an event at the Etihad, was that the £116million club-record signing fancies more of a roaming ‘box-to-box’ role than filling Rodri’s void.

‘I’ve spoken to the manager a few times – he explained the sort of things that I need to do,’ said Anderson. ‘There is a lot of running, a lot of energy. It’s to try and control games. That is what I can do.

‘I’ll see where I get used. Creating things, driving forward or the other role if they ask me to do that. Kevin De Bruyne was always the player I looked up to over the last 10 years. I loved watching him. To be here at the same club and playing where he played is special.’

Ayyoub Bouaddi (right), the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million

There is a feeling that Enzo Fernandez (left) wants to reunite with Enzo Maresca, but for now Elliot Anderson (right) is the man City have identified as the one to run their midfield

City identified Anderson's aggression and punch in the pass as ideal for the way the Premier League operates these days. Maresca has operated with a two-man midfield in his pre-season fixtures – Mateo Kovacic and Reijnders against Atletico Madrid in South Korea on Sunday – and in that system, Anderson would appear as the one who springs forward, chipping in with the sort of goal he scored away at City during a 2-2 draw in March, arriving late.

Kovacic is ahead of Nico Gonzalez in the pecking order and expected to start Sunday’s Community Shield against Arsenal in Cardiff. Both Gonzalez and Kovacic have publicly declared that they do not wish to leave this summer.

The physical demands Maresca places upon his midfielders is huge, with Phil Foden or Rayan Cherki vying for the role pushed up alongside Erling Haaland. Maresca is looking at around half a dozen options as part of the two, with that second runner crucial. The way Reijnders crashed the boxes during their friendlies showcased exactly what is being preached on the training pitch.

‘I’ve taken huge confidence knowing that I can perform on a World Cup stage,’ Anderson said, also admitting that he’s still struggling with England's semi-final defeat by Argentina. ‘Obviously I hadn’t played in anything as big as that yet. I had a big decision to make on who to join and I’m confident I’ve made the right one.’

Sports.title: Arsenal fans left confused by Myles Lewis-Skelly's cryptic celebration after scoring in friendly against Como amid growing uncertainty surrounding his future
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly left Arsenal fans speculating about his future once more after scoring during Wednesday's friendly with Como.

The Gunners won 4-3 on penalties after drawing 1-1 at the Emirates, which saw Lewis-Skelly break the deadlock on 33 minutes.

And as he ran away to celebrate, the 19-year-old wheeled away to a corner of the crowd before spinning to all sections with his hands up in prayer pose as if to apologise.

He followed that up before turning his hands into a love heart before being congratulated by his team-mates.

And after multiple embraces, he then repeatedly patted the Arsenal badge on his chest.

The actions left some Gunners fans confused about the context of it all, amid links to a move to Chelsea or Manchester United this summer.

Goal! Arsenal 1-0 Como. Myles Lewis-Skelly scores and receives a huge cheer from Gooners here at the Emirates pic.twitter.com/Z2APPzjne8 — Layth (@laythy29) August 12, 2026

Myles Lewis-Skelly's goalscoring celebration on Wednesday left some Arsenal fans confused

The 19-year-old has been linked away with a move to Chelsea or Man United this summer

Arsenal fans were left confused on social media behind the meaning of his celebration

'Clearly just feels bad for the s*** rumours that have been going on,' wrote one fan account on X.

'He doesn't need to apologise for nothing [sic]. Proper Hale End,' wrote another Gunners fan.

Another commented: 'He's got nothing to apologise for….!'

As detailed by Daily Mail Sport on Tuesday, Lewis-Skelly has been offered to both Chelsea and Manchester United following the Gunners' capture of Bruno Guimaraes.

The 19-year-old signed a new deal last year following his breakout season, but after limited minutes in Arsenal's Premier League title-winning campaign, there is belief the champions may be willing to move the Hale End product on.

There has been fresh contact with both the Blues and United, among other Premier League clubs, who are assessing whether to make a move for the versatile player.

Lewis-Skelly's minutes at Arsenal could be further limited in the upcoming season, with Guimaraes completing a £75million move from Newcastle last week.

Chelsea are understood to have long held an interest in Lewis-Skelly, but it is unclear whether they will put down an offer.

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson shows true colours as she speaks out about what athletics has cost her
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson shows true colours as she speaks out about what athletics has cost her

Keely Hodgkinson is going for gold at the European Athletics Championships after making numerous sacrifices to get where she is

View 3 Images Keely Hodgkinson has spoken about the downsides of her athletics career (Image: Time to ZOOM In/YouTube)

Keely Hodgkinson has opened up about the sacrifices she made to become one of world athletics' biggest stars. The Olympic 800m champion, 24, has the world at her feet as she looks to become European champion in Birmingham this week.

‌



But it hasn't all been plain sailing for the Manchester-born sensation, who has been forced to swerve some aspects of life most young women take for granted, most notably the time away from family and friends.

‌



Speaking ahead of the European Championships, she was asked what her success had cost her over the years. Hodgkinson told the Time to ZOOM In show with Jeremiah Azu: "I think it costs you a lot of sacrifice from family and friends.

‌



"I travel a lot, so I spend a lot of months of the year not at home. I'm quite fortunate that when I do go back home, my family's there."

Hodgkinson admits her focus on her sport means she hasn't been able to explore other, undiscovered parts of her personality. She added: "Also, some parts of my personality. It [athletics] comes with a lot of discipline and time where you're thinking about how you can be better.

‌

"I'm big on self-improvement, both in personality and physically. You spend so much time on that, that you could have missed out on a whole other part of you that you haven't discovered."

The Briton's showdown with Swiss rival Audrey Werro has been billed as the race of the championships, but Hodgkinson is taking it all in stride. She said: "I don't think I need to put out any kind of statement. I back myself, I don't need to go crazy trying to prove anything.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney lands new Man Utd gig alongside Mark Goldbridge for Gary Neville's Overlap
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney lands new Man Utd gig alongside Mark Goldbridge for Gary Neville's Overlap

Wayne Rooney has taken another step in his punditry career, teaming up with content creator and Manchester United supporter Mark Goldbridge for a new podcast on The Overlap network

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney has a new podcast (Image: Xavier Laine/Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney will host a new Manchester United podcast with YouTube star Mark Goldbridge. Red Devils legend Rooney and Goldbridge - whose real name is Brent Di Cesare - are the faces of Stick to United, a brand-new show from former United captain Gary Neville's network, The Overlap, which is now backed by Disney+.

‌



It was announced on Thursday that Disney+ has bought the rights to broadcast The Overlap's podcast content in a multi-million-pound deal. The move will see Neville's brand compete with Netflix and Gary Lineker's The Rest is Football podcast.

‌



The popular Stick to Football podcast will now have a spinoff show presented by Rooney and Goldbridge. Stick to United will run for 50 episodes, focussing on the Red Devils' trials and tribulations.

‌



After the news broke, Goldridge wrote on X: "Hi Wazza do you want picking up in the morning pal?" The post is a reference to Rooney's iconic tweet that he sent to ex-United team-mate Rio Ferdinand in 2011.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick provides Marcus Rashford transfer update with telling Man Utd statement READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta breaks silence on Myles Lewis-Skelly after Man Utd offered Arsenal star READ MORE :

Goldbridge, 47, is a former police officer from Nottingham. Boasting 1.1million followers on X, he's one of most well-known football fans in the online space, having started his career as a content creator in 2014.

‌



The United Stand now has 2.27m subscribers on YouTube, with viewers from around the globe tuning in to watch Goldbridge's analysis, commentary and frequent rants. Alongside his work for The United Stand, he's co-hosted a radio show on talkSPORT.

In 2024, however, Goldbridge told the Telegraph that he's only been to Old Trafford 'a few times' and once since the pandemic. His loudmouth reputation has made him a divisive figure within the United fan base, particularly irking match-going supporters.

Rooney, meanwhile, is furthering his punditry career, having taken a break from coaching after being sacked by Birmingham City in January 2024. The 40-year-old was a staple of the BBC's World Cup coverage and the star of The Wayne Rooney Show for the corporation last season.

‌



Is this a good move for Wayne Rooney? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Mark Goldbridge is a divisive figure (Image: Jordan Peck/Getty Images)

While both football-centric podcasts on The Overlap network will continue to be available for fans to watch on YouTube, Disney+ will also commission an additional 20 episodes of Stick to Football. Those will be exclusively available to Disney+ subscribers before general release.

‌



Neville launched The Overlap alongside former Sky Sports producer Scott Melvin in 2021. It has grown from Neville conducting one-on-one interviews with star names to weekly shows, and branched off into other sports as seen with Stick to Cricket podcast, presented by England legend Michael Vaughan.

The company said this year that it is attracting 38m views per month on YouTube, having racked up 2.2billion views across all platforms in 2025. Global, the multimedia company which owns radio station LBC and podcasts including The News Agents, purchased a majority stake in The Overlap last year which was followed by the acquisition of Goldbridge's YouTube channels.

‌



After teaming up with Disney+, Neville commented: "We're immensely proud to be partnering with Disney+. It's a partnership that expands our reach without compromising our identity. What's exciting is that we're not changing who we are.

"Our community will continue to enjoy our content in exactly the way they always have through YouTube, while at the same time Disney+'s incredible global streaming audience will now be able to discover and enjoy it too."

Sports.title: Cesc Fabregas opens the door to Arsenal transfers after Max Dowman assessment
Sports.content:
Cesc Fabregas opens the door to Arsenal transfers after Max Dowman assessment

Arsenal were held by Como on Wednesday night as Cesc Fabregas's side impressed - and the former Gunner was full of praise for teenager Max Dowman

View 2 Images Cesc Fabregas was full of praise for Arsenal's academy stars, but insists they need minutes (Image: HaytersTV)

Cesc Fabregas has joked with Arsenal that his Como side are more than happy to take some of their players if it would help Max Dowman to develop further.

‌



The teenage sensation, who became the Premier League's youngest ever scorer last season, got a chance to impress during Arsenal's final pre-season outing against the Italian side at the Emirates.

‌



They are managed by Fabregas, who came through in north London as a teenager, so knows the challenges that will face Dowman in a star-studded outfit. He was hugely impressed by what the youngster offered but made it known to him that he will endure difficult periods during his career.

‌



His greatest challenge currently is getting the minutes he desires. Whether he plays central or out wide, Arsenal have huge depth which means the 16-year-old's opportunities could be limited, with Fabregas confessing that his talent needs to be harnessed - and he's more than happy to help.

Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

The Como boss said: "It's amazing because that's what it's all about. Hale end does an amazing job, there is a lot of talent, but if you don't play this talent, if you don't trust these talents, the talent gets lost. And that's a big shame.

"So I had the chance to say well done to them but keep going, keep pushing yourself because its a big and long career full of ups and downs. They need to accept that not everything will be easy. They need to compete, the play for one of the best clubs and team in the world right now, where even Max, with the talent he's got, its a challenge.

‌



"Its not easy to play at Arsenal because in your position there are some of the best players in the world. So really but, and if they want to give us some players as well, we can take them."

View 2 Images Max Dowman was given another opportunity against Como

Arsenal's line-up featured another academy graduate in Marli Salmon, who came into the defence, and Arteta said: "They played really well. They played with a lot of personality, really connected with the team and against a really good opponent. I think they performed really well.

‌



Arteta and Arsenal's focus will now shift to Sunday's showdown with Manchester City in the season's curtain-raiser, the Community Shield, which will played at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff rather than at Wembley.

He said: "We're looking forward to it. It's a trophy that reflects what we've done in the previous season, winning the Premier League. So we're going to try and win."

Sports.title: Arsenal target's agent 'spotted' at Barcelona as Mikel Arteta stance emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal target's agent 'spotted' at Barcelona as Mikel Arteta stance emerges

The agent of Barcelona defender Jules Kounde has been spotted at the club's training ground, with Arsenal reportedly among the clubs interested in signing the France international

View 2 Images Jules Kounde is reportedly a target for Arsenal (Image: Jose Breton/Getty Images)

The agent of Barcelona star Jules Kounde is reported to have been spotted at the training base of the La Liga club. The update comes amid fresh rumours that Arsenal have expressed an interest in signing the France international before the summer transfer window closes.

‌



Three new signings have been added to Arsenal’s squad that won the Premier League title last season, with Christos Tzolis, Illan Meslier and Bruno Guimaraes all moving to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Arsenal have been linked with potentially strengthening their defensive options this summer, with Kounde, 27, mentioned as a potential target over the last few days.

‌



Spanish outlet SPORT has reported that Arsenal have made their interest in Kounde known, with the defender viewed as a 'perfect fit' for the Gunners given his suitability to Arteta's style and system.

The report also claims that Arteta has firmly backed the potential deal.

Mikel Arteta breaks silence on Myles Lewis-Skelly after Man Utd offered Arsenal star READ MORE :

A fresh development has now emerged regarding Kounde, which could hint that a transfer to Arsenal may genuinely be on the horizon this summer.

‌



According to Jijantes FC, Kounde's agent was spotted arriving at Barcelona's training base, the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper, on Wednesday.

The precise reason of the agent's visit to Barcelona's training ground remains unknown, though the timing has raised eyebrows and led many to speculate whether it is connected to the growing rumours surrounding a possible move to the Emirates.

Kounde was granted an extended summer break by Barcelona following France's run to the World Cup semi-final, but has now rejoined pre-season training with the Spanish club this week.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 2 Images Jules Kounde featured for France at the World Cup this summer (Image: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press via Getty Images)

The centre-back, who is also capable of playing at right-back, featured 47 times for Barcelona last season, predominantly on the right side of a back four.

‌



It remains unclear what Arsenal's intentions are for the remainder of the summer transfer window, with speculation of a potential move for a new defender gathering pace amid doubts surrounding William Saliba's return.

Saliba picked up an injury during the World Cup with France and could face up to five months on the sidelines during his recovery, and may even require surgery. Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa is also being monitored.

Jurrien Timber, meanwhile, has been absent from all four of Arsenal's pre-season friendlies so far this summer, and travelled back to England from the club's training base in Spain earlier this month.

Article continues below

The Gunners have emphasised that this decision formed part of Timber's rehabilitation programme rather than a fresh injury setback.

Sports.title: Casemiro stunned as Lionel Messi returns hours after emotional letter about dad's death
Sports.content:
Casemiro stunned as Lionel Messi returns hours after emotional letter about dad's death

Lionel Messi returned to competitive action for the first time since the death of his father and former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro was left stunned

View 2 Images Casemiro and Lionel Messi are now teammates at Inter Miami (Image: Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images)

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro was left in awe of Lionel Messi after the Inter Miami star's surprise comeback. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner and Barcelona legend returned to competitive action days after the tragic passing of his father.

‌



The Brazilian spoke highly of his new teammate following his return in Miami's 3-2 defeat to Mexican side Leon in the Leagues Cup. Messi came on as a second-half substitute in his first outing since the passing of his father Jorge on Saturday at the age of 68. The comeback from the Argentina star resonated with Casemiro who heaped praise on the attacker.

‌



He said: "He's an example. I'm sure he's going through a very difficult time but his commimtent, not only to the players but also the club was incredible.

‌



"I've never seen anything like it in my life. All I can do is thank him for being here. That's why he's so great and one of the best in history, if not the best. We have to take our hats off to him and say thank you, continue supporting him and encouraging him."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Michael Carrick provides Marcus Rashford transfer update with telling Man Utd statement READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta breaks silence on Myles Lewis-Skelly after Man Utd offered Arsenal star READ MORE :

The pair now finally share the same dressing room following their mammoth clashes during Casemiro's time at Real Madrid. The 34-year-old enjoyed a phenomenal final season at Old Trafford, turning in his most prolific goalscoring season for United, but found himself as a free agent at the end of the campaign.

‌



Inter Miami won the race to the veteran midfielder's signature, beating Major League Soccer (MLS) rivals LA Galaxy. Messi hinted at the prospect of retirement following the death of his father.

The 39-year-old has faced growing speculation over the potential to end his glittering career and he dropped a major hint in paying tribute to his late dad. He wrote on Instagram : "I don't know what I'm going to do without you, I don't know how to go on.

"I just played football, and now I have serious doubts that I'll be able to keep doing it for much longer. You were by my side from the beginning; the end was so close. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?

‌



"I know your happiness came from seeing your family well, your wife, your children, and, above all, without the others finding out, seeing me play... It was always like that from the time I was little. You took me to every training session as soon as you got home from work. My mom took me to many of them because you were working.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi with his late father Jorge (Image: X)

"Obviously, you never missed a match. How you suffered watching me and how you enjoyed it, even though you never gave me much praise. You were a father, a friend, and an agent.

‌



"You were always the person you needed to be in every moment, and you were never wrong about anything. Beyond some reproaches or arguments, you were always right. In the end, things always turned out the way you said.

"I'm going to miss you so much, but you'll always be present, especially in my children's upbringing, because I teach and raise them the way you did me. Rest in peace and watch over us from above like you did here. Thank you for everything. I love you, Dad."

Inter Miami bowed out of the Leagues Cup after their defeat to the Liga Mexico side. Leon equalised shortly after Messi's introduction after Daniel Pinter's opener.

‌



Parity was short-lived as Yannick Bright restored their lead three minutes later. But the visitors fought back through Juan Dominuez while Daniel Arcila doubled his tally for the evening, sending them three clear at the top with their unbeaten record.

Casemiro played the entirety of the match but suffered successive defeats for the first time since moving to North America.

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer deal moves one step closer after official announcement
Sports.content:
Arsenal transfer deal moves one step closer after official announcement

Arsenal frontman Gabriel Jesus could be edging closer to a move to Napoli after the Italian side raised funds via the sale of Romelu Lukaku, who has headed to Turkey

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus is being linked with an Arsenal exit (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Arsenal's Gabriel Jesus could be edging closer to the exit door after Napoli were able to offload Romelu Lukaku - leaving them free to pursue the Brazilian.

‌



Jesus has been at the Emirates since 2022 but has slipped down the pecking order and is about to enter the final year of his deal. Jesus has been a worthy contributor, but hasn't provided the goals that the team has been seeking.

‌



Mikel Arteta has signed Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz, who can both lead the line, and remains in the market for more firepower. It leaves Jesus free to leave if he can find a club and the Italians could offer him a route out of north London.

‌



Jesus has been playing in the Premier League since leaving his boyhood club Palmeiras, but a move to Napoli could see him continue to fight for titles with new boss Max Allegri eyeing up new recruits.

Mikel Arteta breaks silence on Myles Lewis-Skelly after Man Utd offered Arsenal star READ MORE :

Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

The outfit from Naples have undergone a reshuffle which saw Antonio Conte leave after two seasons at the helm and now Lukaku has been moved on, joining Turkish side Fenerbahce. The ex-Chelsea man had helped Napoli win Serie A in 2025 but was deemed surplus to requirements.

The club still need to raise further funds, but Lukaku's exit provides a welcome boost with Arsenal seeking between £18million - £20m if they are to let Jesus leave, reports Sky Sports.

‌



Napoli have just made their move for Rasmus Hojlund permanent after he spent last year on loan at the club. They also boast Kevin De Bruyne and Scott McTominay, who was named the best player in Serie A the year before last.

View 2 Images Romelu Lukaku has joined Fenerbahce - allowing Napoli to pursue the Brazilian

Jesus returned to Arsenal action at the end of 2025 after spending nearly 12 months on the sidelines due to an ACL injury he sustained in an FA Cup defeat to Manchester United. That meant he went 332 days without playing for the Gunners.

Article continues below

Arteta refused to entertain his exit back in January and claimed: "A player of his quality, a player who has given us so much and when he comes with the energy he did the other day, he is certainly a player who has to be pushing and aiming [to start], that's for sure."

Sports.title: Chelsea set Man City strict deadline to complete £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer
Sports.content:
Chelsea set Man City strict deadline to complete £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer

Chelsea have made it clear to Manchester City that they had to bid for Enzo Fernandez before the week is out if they want to have any chance of signing the midfielder

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has been linked with a move away from Chelsea this summer (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Manchester City have been told they need to submit a bid for Enzo Fernandez by 5pm on Friday - otherwise Chelsea will refuse to do business.

‌



City are among those keen on the Argentine midfielder, who has a good relationship with new boss Enzo Maresca, but the Blues want to avoid a saga that drags on until the end of the transfer window. The west Londoners want to ensure they know whether their player is sticking around, or could feasibly leave.

‌



They want new manager Xabi Alonso and his players to be able to focus on the new season ahead and Sky Sports reports that Chelsea insist any buyers have had two months to begin negotiations for Fernandez.

‌



Chelsea value Fernandez at £120m - meaning any move from City would need them to break their own transfer record for the second time this summer - and he has six years left on his contract.

Arsenal reignite Ezri Konsa transfer hopes but face massive Aston Villa problem READ MORE :

PSG chief drops transfer bombshell on Liverpool target Bradley Barcola READ MORE :

City's interest in Fernandez is closely linked to the future or Rodri. The Spanish World Cup winner has been at the Etihad since 2019 but Barcelona are keen and have seen a £40m bid rejected. The midfielder is keen to return home before his career is over and, should that happen this summer, City will need a replacement.

They have already landed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who enjoyed a stellar World Cup.

‌



Fernandez was dropped by Chelsea for two games in April after he admitted he would welcome living in Madrid, but Real Madrid themselves have moved to distance themselves from a move this summer. The player and his agent would later apologised for those comments.

View 2 Images New Man City Enzo Maresca has a good relationship with the Argentine

Relations with City and Chelsea have been stressed in recent months, owing largely to Maresca's move to Manchester. He admitted that he'd held talks with his new employers whilst he was still in charge at the Blues as the Etihad hierarchy looked to life beyond Pep Guardiola.

Article continues below

That saw Chelsea make the decision to axe Maresca in January and City eventually had to pay Chelsea £17m in compensation to appoint Maresca this summer.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
