World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: Watch: When gunman tried to assassinate Sukhbir Badal at Golden Temple in 2024
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Sukhbir Singh Badalâs Thursday attack in Nanded marks the second serious attempt on the Shiromani Akali Dal leaderâs life. The SAD leader was also attacked two years ago at the Golden Temple when a gunman opened fire at him while Badal was serving religious punishment at the shrine.

On December 4, 2024, Badal was attacked at the entrance of the temple, where he was seated in a wheelchair because of his fractured leg, during a penance ordered by the Akal Takht. Video footage from the incident shows the moment the attacker overpowered him within seconds.

The footage showed him dressed in a blue sewadar uniform. He was stationed at the temple entrance as part of the punishment pronounced by the Akal Takht over alleged misconduct during his tenure from 2007 to 2017.

As Badal sat with a placard around his neck, a man who was later identified as Narayan Singh Chaura approached him and opened fire. The attempt, however, was foiled almost immediately.

In the clip, right after the gunman pulled out the weapon, an alert sewadar, believed to be a volunteer associated with an Akali leader, intervened and pushed the assailantâs arm upward as he attempted to fire. The bullet was discharged harmlessly into the air, and the attacker was quickly overpowered by volunteers and others present at the scene.





Police personnel stationed at the shrine also moved in and apprehended Chaura on the spot. Confirming the swift response, ADCP Harpal Singh said, âNo one was injured in the attack.â

It was not long after the attempted attack that other sewadars present at the scene assembled together to create a human shield around Badal.

Despite the dramatic shooting attempt, Badal remained calm.

Still seated in his wheelchair, he continued performing his duties as a sewadar, holding a spear and staying at the temple entrance after the assailant had been detained.

In a separate clip, the shooter could be seen being overpowered by the crowd. The people holding the man can be heard asking him his motive for opening fire on the SAD leader.

The religious punishment had been announced on December 2, 2024, by Sikh high priests for Badal and other Akali leaders in connection with incidents of sacrilege and the pardon granted to controversial Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim. The tankhah was part of a reconciliation process led by Sikh religious authorities to address long-standing grievances within the community.

Rijiju targets Congress over disruptions

NEW DELHI: Parliamentâs Monsoon Session ended on Thursday with both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha being adjourned sine die, bringing to a close a session marked by repeated disruptions and protests by opposition parties.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the session was successful in terms of legislative business, with 12 Bills passed, but criticised the quality of debates and discussions.Addressing a press briefing, he said the government was not satisfied with the level of parliamentary discussion during the session.Rijiju said Lok Sabha productivity stood at 19% of the total allotted time, while Rajya Sabha recorded 39%.âThe Monsoon Session concluded today. We view it from two perspectives. In terms of business, it was a very successful session; we passed a total of 12 bills. However, from the perspective of debate and discussion, it was not as successful,â Rijiju said.He alleged that opposition parties repeatedly disrupted proceedings and avoided discussions offered by the government.âBased on my parliamentary experience and what I have seen in my life, this is the first time the Opposition was running away from discussions,â he said.According to Rijiju, 11 Bills were passed in the Lok Sabha without discussion, while one Bill underwent discussion. He said the Bills were discussed in the Rajya Sabha, although Congress and some other Opposition members staged a walkout.Rijiju said the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Bill was the only legislation to undergo a full discussion in the Lok Sabha during the session.âOnly one bill, addressing the issue of paper leaks and unfair means in examinations, underwent a full discussion in the Lok Sabha,â he said.The legislation, which seeks to prevent unfair means in public examinations, was also discussed in the Rajya Sabha before being passed during the session.The Monsoon Session, which began on July 20, witnessed prolonged disruptions in both Houses.Opposition protests initially focused on the NEET paper leak and alleged irregularities involving donations to the Ram temple in Ayodhya.The opposition later sought discussions on police action against students protesting over the NEET issue and demanded statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah.The government offered a discussion on the NEET paper leak and related issues, along with a reply from Shah, but the proposal was rejected by the Congress. A similar proposal made on Wednesday also failed to break the deadlock.Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition wanted answers over allegations concerning police action against protesting students and criticised the prospect of a speech by Shah.Rijiju accused Congress MPs of reducing their parliamentary role to sloganeering and creating disruptions.âAnother observation I have made is that Congress MPs seem to believe their primary role is merely to raise slogans and create a ruckus with placards and banners,â he said.He also said disruptions had particularly affected newly elected MPs by limiting opportunities for debate and discussion.âAs the minister of parliamentary affairs, I feel genuinely sorry for the Congress MPs, especially the new ones,â Rijiju said. âHow can they learn if there are no debates or discussions?âHe expressed hope that opposition parties would reflect on their conduct and participate in more substantive debates when Parliament reconvenes for the Winter Session.The session also saw counter-protests between BJP and INDIA bloc MPs at the Makar Dwar steps of the Parliament complex.

World.title: 'Bid to weaken stir': Students accuse Jharkhand govt of withholding Devendra Mahto's health details
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who is on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations, remains hospitalised at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi, with protesting students alleging that the state government is withholding information about his health to weaken their agitation.

Meanwhile, former Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Thursday visited Mahto at the hospital and enquired about his health.

Mahto has been on hunger strike for 11 days and is undergoing treatment after he was injured during a police lathi-charge on August 10. The wider protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants entered its 20th day on Thursday, with students continuing their agitation at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.

Students allege govt hiding Mahtoâs health details

The protesting students have alleged that the government is not allowing them to meet Mahto at the hospital and is withholding details about his health.

Mahto was moved to Sadar Hospital by the administration late Monday evening after police used force to disperse thousands of aspirants who had marched towards the state assembly.

Raghubar Das meets Mahto

In a post on X, Mahto said: "Former Chief Minister of Jharkhand Raghubar Das ji reached the hospital and inquired about my well-being, while also assuring support for our movement."

Das had on Wednesday threatened to go on a hunger strike if the demand for a CBI probe was not fulfilled within a week.





He has also sought compensation of Rs 1 crore each for the families of 19 people who died during the 2024 excise constable physical examination.

The BJP has accused the Hemant Soren government of suppressing the student movement, while the Congress has accused the saffron party of politicising the agitation and alleged that it brought workers from outside Jharkhand to disrupt the protests.

On Tuesday, in a message shared on social media, Mahto said "My body is undergoing treatment in the hospital bed, but my soul and resolve are at the Satyagraha site where students and youth are engaged in a just struggle for their future.

The indefinite hunger strike continues on its 11th day in Sadar Hospital."

Mahto has also sought permission from the hospital authorities to return to the protest site. In a handwritten application to the Civil Surgeon, he said being separated from the protesting students was causing him greater distress than his physical ailments.

He cited his responsibility towards thousands of students protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and sought permission to rejoin them.

The protesters have been demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. They have alleged that their demands have not been fully accepted by the state government.

These creators are not only building communities online but are also amplifying local stories, inspiring millions and showcasing Uttar Pradesh's talent on the national and global stage.

The event will also feature engaging fireside chats on themes such as "Storytellers of a New Bharat" and "Beyond Followers", examining how creators are moving beyond metrics to create meaningful impact, influence culture and build sustainable careers.

World.title: Leave what you can, take what you need: community fridges in Visakhapatnam from August 15
World.content:
Visakhapatnam city police have launched another community-driven initiative to ensure that no one in the city goes to bed hungry, by setting up ‘community fridges’.

On a pilot basis, the fridges are being installed at Asilmetta, Jagadamba Junction, Maddilapalem, Gopalapatnam and Gajuwaka, where members of the public can donate surplus fresh food. People in need can take the food from the fridges free of cost.

Speaking to The Hindu, Commissioner of Police Shanka Brata Bagchi said the project would be formally launched on August 15, Independence Day. The project is aimed at encouraging community participation in addressing hunger and ensuring that surplus food reaches those who need it most.

“People can place fresh food in the community fridges, while those in need can take it,” Mr. Bagchi said. He said only fresh and safe-to-consume food should be donated, to prevent any health risks to beneficiaries.

He said arrangements were being made to monitor the fridges and ensure their proper functioning. CCTV cameras are being installed at the locations, and police personnel will be deployed to oversee the facilities.

Mr. Bagchi said the response to the pilot would be assessed before extending the programme to more locations across the city.

The community fridges initiative is part of the Visakhapatnam city police’s broader focus on community-oriented policing and services for vulnerable sections.

The city police had earlier launched ‘Operation Jyothirgamayee’, aimed at identifying and assisting destitute persons. Under it, thousands of vulnerable people were traced and assisted. Some were sheltered at GVMC night shelters, while others were reunited with their families or admitted to hospitals for treatment. It also helped several people find employment, and was intended to restore their dignity and provide them with an opportunity to lead meaningful lives.

“Seeing people begging or sleeping on the streets was heart-wrenching. No one should have to beg to survive. Every human being deserves to live with dignity,” Mr. Bagchi said.

World.title: Delhi women cops go undercover as decoys, detain over 1 lakh for harassment, molestation
World.content:
New Delhi

Over a year since their launch, Delhi Police’s Shishtachar squads have detained about 1.05 lakh people during 15,077 drives for street harassment, molestation, and other offences against women in public places.

The initiative was launched in March 2025, modelled after Uttar Pradesh’s ‘Anti-Romeo’ squads, following a Bharatiya Janata Party poll promise from the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections.

In 2025, the squads conducted 10,449 drives and detained 65,615 people. This year, they have already carried out 4,628 drives, detaining another 40,015 people, taking the cumulative figure to 1,05,630.

There are 30 Shishtachar squads across Delhi, with each squad comprising 11 core personnel: an Inspector, a Sub-Inspector, four women police officers and five male police officers, besides personnel from Special Staff or Anti-Auto Theft Squad for technical assistance.

The teams have women personnel in plain clothes to identify perpetrators and detain them. The squads conduct checks in high-footfall and vulnerable locations, including schools and colleges, malls, as well as isolated or poorly lit areas, looking for men who harass women, make inappropriate remarks, record women without consent, loiter suspiciously and create disturbances. A woman official, involved in the operations, said that there are instances when men start following or misbehaving with us as well but the team detains them immediately.

Hari Krishan, Inspector with the Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC) unit, said, “Our team in plain clothes boards the bus from one station and stays onboard for three or four stations, or all along the route, depending on the need. There are several instances where men, not realising that the woman is a cop, end up making a move or behaving inappropriately with them.”

The operations are based on a combination of tip-offs, ground intelligence, direct observation and patterns emerging from previous complaints, said one of the officials said.

In most cases, men are taken to the local police station and a Daily Diary or General Diary entry is made. They are then counselled in the presence of their families and let off after a warning. Serious cases of sexual harassment or molestation result in FIRs and further investigation, said the official.

“The idea is to ensure women feel safe. They must know we are among them at all times if they are in need,” the official added.

World.title: Tata Trusts accepts N. Chandrasekaran’s resignation, initiates process to find successor
World.content:
The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, which controls 27.9% holdings in Tata Sons, has accepted the resignation of Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran and initiated process to search for his successor.

“On 12th August 2026, our nominee directors received an email from Mr. N. Chandrasekaran, Chairman, Tata Sons Private Limited, wherein he conveyed his decision to not offer himself for re-appointment as Chairman upon the expiry of his current tenure on 20th February 2027,” Tata Trusts said in a statement.

“The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) respects Mr. Chandrasekaran’s decision not to offer himself for re-appointment. We place on record our deepest appreciation for his contribution and stewardship of Tata Sons and the Tata group over the past decade,” it said.

“We thank him for his immense contribution during a period of significant change, growth and transformation across the Group,” the statement said.

“The Trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust have passed a resolution to initiate the setting up of a Selection Committee as soon as possible in accordance with the Articles of Association of Tata Sons, for the purpose of recommending a person for appointment as the new Chairman of the Board of Directors,” the statement said.

“We extend our full support to Tata Sons in ensuring a smooth, timely and orderly transition of leadership, consistent with the values and long-term interests of Tata Sons and the Tata group,” it added.

World.title: Himanta appeals for peace along Assam-Arunachal border, says boundaries can never divide hearts
World.content:
With a fresh clash reported from the Assam-Arunachal Pradesh border, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Thursday (August 13, 2026) appealed to both sides to maintain peace and said no boundary can divide the hearts of the people who have been living like brothers and sisters for generations.

A fresh clash erupted between protestors from Assam and Arunachal Pradesh in Dhemaji district, forcing the police from the neighbouring State to fire in the air to control the mob even as the indefinite economic blockade against the Himalayan State entered its second day.

"I appeal to the people of Assam and Arunachal to maintain peace and harmony. Boundaries may define our States, but they can never divide our hearts," Mr. Sarma said in a post on X.

Chief Minister Pema Khandu on Thursday appealed to people of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam to maintain peace, harmony and mutual respect amid tension following a firing incident along the inter-state border and welcomed the “positive and reassuring” statement of his Assam counterpart Himanta Biswa Sarma.

Tagging his Arunachal Pradesh counterpart Pema Khandu and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, the Assam CM said that the two Northeastern States share a bond that goes far beyond boundaries.

Assam-Arunachal Prades border differences

Mr. Sarma stressed that the two states have resolved most of their border differences through dialogue and friendship in recent years.

"Only 52 villages remain, and both governments will continue discussions in the same spirit to resolve the dispute completely," he added.

Arunachal Pradesh was a centrally-administered region initially after Independence and became a Union Territory later, before attaining full statehood in 1987.

After Arunachal Pradesh achieved Statehood, a tripartite committee was appointed, which recommended transferring certain territories from Assam to Arunachal Pradesh. Assam contested this, and the matter is in the Supreme Court.

Assam and Arunachal Pradesh share a 804.1-km border in Udalguri, Sonitpur, Biswanath, Lakhimpur, Dhemaji, Tinsukia, Dibrugarh and Charaideo districts, and 12 of the adjoining State.

There are 1,200 points of dispute along the inter-State border between the two States.

The Assam government on July 29 told the State Assembly that Arunachal Pradesh has encroached upon 16,144.01 hectares of land. Out of this encroached land, Arunachal Pradesh is claiming 858.91 sq km.

Both the States have constituted 12 regional committees to resolve the border disputes, and are taking steps to resolve these issues based on recommendations of these committees, which have jointly toured the areas and held consultations with stakeholders.

A Namsai Declaration was signed by the Chief Ministers of the two States on July 15, 2022, setting in motion measures to resolve differences in 123 villages of Assam claimed by Arunachal Pradesh.

An MoU in this regard was later signed by the two CMs in the presence of the Union Home minister in the national capital on April 20, 2023.

Out of the 123 villages claimed by Arunachal Pradesh, the differences in 71 villages have been resolved, and the process is on to address the issues in the remaining 52 villages.

World.title: Putin pays his first visit to Pacific island chain claimed by Japan, drawing protest from Tokyo
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday (August 13, 2026) visited the Kuril Islands, a Russian-controlled Pacific island chain also claimed by Japan, for the first time, drawing protests from Tokyo.

Mr. Putin visited a fish plant, a hospital and a school on Iturup, one of the chain's southernmost islands. He also briefly spoke to local residents and met with the governor of Russia's Sakhalin region, Valery Limarenko.

Japan asserts territorial rights to the four southernmost islands of the chain, which it calls the Northern Territories. The Soviet Union took them from Japan in the final days of World War II, and the dispute kept the countries from signing a peace treaty formally ending their hostilities.

Decades of diplomatic efforts to negotiate a settlement haven't produced any visible results. Moscow over the years has also beefed up its military presence on the Kuril Islands in moves that appeared to underscore its firm stance in the dispute.

Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said his country “strongly protests” against Putin's visit to Iturup, which Japan calls Etorofu. “The Northern Territories, including Etorofu (Iturup) Island, are Japan's inherent territory both historically and from the perspective of international law,” Mr. Motegi said in a statement.

Japan also protested in 2021 when Russia's Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin visited Iturup.

Mr. Putin in recent days has visited several regions in Russia's Siberia and the Far East. Before coming to Iturup, the Russian president stopped on Sakhalin Island to attend the final part of the drills by Russia's Pacific Fleet.

Speaking aboard a warship that was taking part in the naval exercises, Putin said on Wednesday (August 12) that the current status of the Kuril Islands “is enshrined in international documents as a reality that arose following the outcome of the World War II.” “But even here, Russia was prepared to seek a solution with the goal of concluding a peace treaty with Japan,” he said.

The Russian leader said that in the past, Moscow “had developed constructive relations with a number of Japanese leaders, including the tragically deceased former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, who did much to bring Japan and Russia closer together, to align our positions.”

Mr. Putin said the position of Japan, which imposed sanctions on Russia after its sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022, has since changed.

Still, Russia is ready “to cooperate with all its neighbors, including Japan and other states in the region,” the Russian president said.

World.title: Singapore’s Indian-origin opposition MP struck off as lawyer over case of lying in Parliament
World.content:
Singapore’s leading opposition politician Pritam Singh was on Thursday (August 13, 2026) struck off the roll of advocates over his criminal conviction for lying to a parliamentary committee.

The striking-off was handed to the 50-year-old Indian-origin politician by the the Court of Three Judges, the city-state's highest disciplinary body for the legal profession, The Straits Times newspaper reported.

Mr. Singh, the secretary-general of the Workers’ Party (WP) and a Member of Parliament (MP), is a non-practising lawyer.

On March 4, the Law Society of Singapore started disciplinary proceedings against Mr. Singh in compliance with the Legal Profession Act.

Under the Act, a lawyer can be struck off, suspended from practice for up to five years, censured, fined up to SGD 100,000, or given a combination of these sanctions.

The proceedings were based on information received from the Attorney-General’s Chambers that Mr. Singh had been convicted of offences involving “fraud or dishonesty”, according to the report.

Pritam Singh convicted of lying

Mr. Singh, a former Leader of the Opposition, was convicted by a district court in February 2025 on two counts of lying under oath to the Committee of Privileges. This was related to his colleague and a former WP MP Raeesah Khan’s lie in parliament in 2021 about details of a sexual assault case that she alleged was mishandled by the police in Singapore.

In December 2025, Mr. Singh lost his appeal to the High Court against his conviction and paid his SGD 14,000 fine.

Mr. Singh was stripped of the LoP title in January this year.

Delivering the court's judgment, Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon said it was undisputed that dishonesty was an "integral element" of Mr. Singh's offences.

Mr. Singh has led the WP since 2018. The party has 10 elected MPs and two Non-Constituency MPs in the 108-seat parliament. The rest of the seats are held by the People’s Action Party, which has ruled Singapore ever since independence.

World.title: T-Hub launches ‘deep tech’ founder fellowship, selects 14 startups for first cohort
World.content:
Startup incubator T-Hub has launched Blueprint, a 12-month fellowship programme for deep tech startup founders, aimed at helping them scale their ventures.

Customised support based on a startup’s stage and sector will be provided, especially to help the founders build the operating and commercial foundations needed for growth. Blueprint was unveiled on the sidelines of an event in which Secretary to the government of India’s Technology Development Board Rajesh Kumar Pathak participated, the incubator said in a release on Thursday (August 13, 2026).

T-Hub also announced the selection of 14 startups for the inaugural cohort. Blueprint is part of its efforts to strengthen Hyderabad as a base for deep tech founders and deepen its role as a co-builder for startups, it said.

“A founder today can build from anywhere, so a hub must do more than provide a place to work. At T-Hub, we believe that means co-building with them and Blueprint puts this into practice,” CEO Kavikrut said.

The first cohort comprises Kritsnam, ArtusAI, Litemed, Zodhya, Arkle Energy, Sensehealth, Vahn, Buildwright, Sanyark Space, Semex AI, Pavakah Energy, Vecros, Portl and Storyvord.

Blueprint will assist the founders prepare for fundraising through VC-ready pitches and organised financial, legal and business documentation. T-Hub will also facilitate investor interactions, enterprise contracts and international exposure.

Mr. Pathak highlighted the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund, and how it is poised to be a crucial capital pathway for Indian startups developing deep tech with significant economic and strategic potential.

TDB is a part of the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

World.title: Security beefed up in Chennai for Independence Day celebrations
World.content:
In view of the 80th Independence Day celebrations on Saturday (August 15, 2026), the Greater Chennai City Police has made elaborate security arrangements across the city. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay will hoist the national flag at the ramparts of Fort St. George in Chennai and deliver the Independence Day address.

A five-tier security arrangement involving police officers and personnel has been put in place at Fort St. George and its surrounding areas, in accordance with Chennai Police Commissioner A. Amalraj’s directions. Special security duties have been organised under the supervision of Additional Commissioners Kapil Kumar C. Saratkar (North), K.S. Narendra Nair (South), and B. Shamoondeshwari (Traffic).

Mr. Amalraj said as a precautionary measure, additional police teams have been deployed at Chennai airport, railway stations, bus terminals, bus and metro stations, commercial complexes, beaches, places of worship, and other important locations frequented by VIPs. Intensive checks and surveillance are being carried out at these places.

The police are also conducting checks at hotels and lodges across Chennai. The public has been advised to inform the police about any suspicious movements or unattended vehicles. The Commissioner said patrolling has been intensified across the city using four-wheelers and two-wheelers. The police have set up barricades at key locations and are conducting intensive vehicle checks. Additional personnel have also been deployed at important locations for round-the-clock surveillance and security, said Mr. Amalraj.

Traffic arrangements

The Greater Chennai City Traffic Police has also announced traffic regulations to be implemented on Independence Day at St. George Fort and surrounding areas from 6 a.m. until the function is over.

The police said the stretch of Kamarajar Salai from Labour Statue upto RBI Subway North on Rajaji Salai and Flag Staff Road will be closed for all vehicular traffic, except for vehicles with red and purple colour car passes.

The red and purple colour car pass-holder vehicles plying on Kamarajar Salai before 8.10 a.m. will take Rajaji Salai and alight outside the Secretariat in-gate. The vehicles will then be parked inside the Secretariat at their respective places – in front of Japan House, NCC Office, Army Parade Ground, Minister Parking, the front and rear sides of the Namakkal Building, and near Fort Museum.

After 8.10 a.m. the above pass-holders will not have entry via War Memorial, and the vehicles will be diverted onto Flag Staff Road, Wallajah Point, Muthusamy Point, Muthusamy Road, NFS Road, Parrys Corner (U-turn) RBI Subway, upto the out-gate of the Secretariat. The vehicles will be parked at PWD Parking.

Blue and pink colour car pass holders plying before 8.10 a.m. on Kamarajar Salai will not have entry via War Memorial, and the vehicles will be diverted onto Flag Staff Road, Wallajah Point, Muthusamy Point, Muthusamy Road, NFS Road, Parrys Corner (U-turn) RBI Subway, upto the Secretariat out-gate. The vehicles will be parked at PWD Parking.

After 8.10 a.m., the above pass holders will not have entry via Labour Statue, and the vehicles will be diverted into Wallajah Salai - Anna Salai - Muthusamy Bridge - Muthusamy Road - R.A. Mandram and NFS Road to reach Parrys Corner and take a U-turn to RBI Subway, upto the Secretariat out-gate. The vehicles will be parked at PWD Parking.

The vehicles of journalists cannot be parked at the PWD Parking. If the parking is full, they will return via RBI Subway, NSC Bose Road, Esplanade Road, R.A. Mandram, Muthusamy Road, Flag Staff Road, and enter through Island Ground 6th Gate and park their vehicles.

The police vehicles below the rank of ADSP to police personnel can enter through Island Ground 6th gate for parking.

The vehicles coming from Anna Salai and intending to proceed towards Parrys Corner and Kamarajar Salai via Flag Staff Road may travel via Muthusamy Bridge - Muthusamy Road - R.A. Mandram - NFS Road to reach Parrys Corner and Anna Salai - Wallajah Road to reach Kamarajar Salai respectively.

Those vehicles without passes will be allowed upto the Labour Statue and then diverted into Wallajah Salai, Anna Salai, and enter Island Ground 9th gate to park their vehicles.

If the parking is full inside Island Grounds 9th gate, those vehicles without passes will alight near Labour Statue and they will be parked on Anna Salai (outgoing side), Omandurar Hospital, Sivanandha Salai (one-side road parking), Anna Swimming Pool, Foreshore Road (upto Seerani Arangam), Victoria Hostel Road, and MRTS Parking.

World.title: Pakistan, Norway reaffirm resolve to strengthen bilateral ties, expand engagement in defence and security
World.content:
Pakistan and Norway on Thursday reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation in defence and security.

Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide, who is on a two-day visit to Pakistan, called on Chief of Defence Forces and the Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, with the two leaders reiterating their resolve to further strengthen bilateral ties and expand engagement in defence and security, according to a statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

The two sides discussed matters of “mutual interest, regional security, and bilateral relations”.

During the meeting, Field Marshal Munir highlighted “Pakistan’s perspective on global peace and regional stability” and stressed the “importance of cooperation and collaborative efforts to address common security challenges”.

The Norwegian foreign minister appreciated the “professional role” played by the Pakistan Armed Forces “in promoting regional peace and stability”.

Earlier in the day, Eide addressed a press conference alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad, during which he lauded Pakistan’s mediatory role in the US-Iran conflict, saying it was a “service to the world and hence, also to us”.

“I also really want to reiterate our strong support for the very important role that Pakistan has taken in this dramatic war that started on February 28 with the US-Israel attack on Iran,” he said, recalling that Norway was one of the Western countries that was “clearest and earliest” in stating that the war was a violation of international rules.

“If we stand up for international law, it has to apply to everyone, everywhere, all the time,” he stressed.

He said that while Norway had “significant disagreements with Iran on other issues, they also have the right to be protected as a state”.

Referring to Pakistan’s mediatory role in the ongoing conflict, he said he realised how difficult mediation and facilitation of parleys between the two sides could be.

“I know what a massive task you were taking on when you offered Islamabad not only as the venue but also as the facilitator of these talks,” he said, lauding Pakistan’s civilian and military leadership for their efforts.

“What you have been doing is really a service to the world, and hence, also to us.”

The Norwegian foreign minister said Pakistan’s mediation efforts also mattered to his country as it was a large shipping nation.

“We share an interest in open sea lanes and the ability to trade in the high seas, and to respect the Constitution of the Oceans […] Whatever emerges from this tragic and unnecessary war in Gulf, we need to protect the principle of the free passage,” he explained. “And I am so happy we see completely eye to eye [on this],” he remarked.

The visiting minister added that his message to “anyone involved out there in the conflict is that this issue of free passage and an open strait is not an issue for the warring parties alone. It is a global issue that we have a shared interest in promoting”.

He said he had discussed other regional issues during the visit as well, ranging from the Kashmir issue to Afghanistan.

Moreover, Eide said, he was glad to learn more about a recently signed defence pact between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia in Makkah.

“These are three countries with whom Norway has very good and close relations,” he noted.

At the outset of his address, Eide said he was honoured to be in Pakistan, saying the last time a Norwegian foreign minister visited Pakistan was 10 years ago.

“So it was about time,” he remarked. “I promised you many months ago that I would come, and today, I live up to my promise. I was looking forward to this visit, which is short but very effective.”

Eide said there was a “strong partnership” between Norway and Pakistan, as well as the people of the two countries.

“We have a sizeable diaspora of Pakistani descent […] Many of them are in key positions of politics and society and are a very welcome contribution to our country; and the fact that we have so many people who know these two countries intimately is yet another argument for strengthening our economic ties,” he added.

The Norwegian foreign minister further said that Oslo and Islamabad were discussing strengthening economic ties “in the context of specifics” and enhancing trade ties in more structural ways.

He also mentioned climate change and floods in Pakistan, saying that the two sides agreed it was a foreign policy issue.

“And if you need one additional argument for stopping wars apart from relieving suffering and ending economic harm, it is that mankind should collectively try to focus on the real issues that require real cooperative action,” he said.

Eide mentioned combatting nature loss, climate change, promoting global health and fighting poverty in this connection, adding that all of them were on his agenda for discussions during the visit.

Speaking before him, Dar said the two countries had agreed to enhance their ties and cooperation in all areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, education, defence, climate change, IT and maritime affairs.

He said Pakistan greatly valued its relations with Norway and looked forward to further strengthening these ties in the days, weeks and months to come.

Moreover, he continued, bilateral political consultations (BPC) between the two countries had become a regular feature. “We are looking forward to hosting the next round of BPC in Islamabad later this year in the winter,” he said.

Dar said the two sides also agreed that bilateral trade between Norway and Pakistan was “below the potential of both economies and needs to be enhanced through effective measures”.

“Pakistan offers enormous investment opportunities to Norwegian companies, and it is heartening to see many leading Norwegian companies investing in Pakistan.

“A renowned Norwegian company, Yara International, is establishing a joint venture in plant nutrition with the Fauji Fertiliser company. I hope this initiative will be a trailblazer for many more future projects between our two great countries,” he added.

Dar termed Pakistan’s partnership with Norway in the field of technology “a success story”.

“Pakistan’s IT exports to Norway have grown more than five-fold in the last two years, and I have no doubt that this is only the beginning.”

He further stated that the two sides also agreed on the expedient finalisation of various agreements and memoranda of understanding (MoU).

On climate change, he said there was a convergence of perspectives between the two countries.

“It is heartening to note that Pakistan and Norway signed the MoU under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on April 1 this year,” he said, adding that the two sides also held talks on cooperation in maritime affairs.

He said he had told the visiting dignitary that Pakistan was “one of the world’s largest ship recycling facilities, and our strategic location makes it the most competitive and nearest recycling destination in this maritime region for ships coming from Norway”.

Dar thanked Norway’s maritime authorities for their support in capacity building and providing technical training for Pakistan’s shipbreaking industry in line with the Hong Kong International Convention.

He added that Pakistan and Norway had agreed to enhance people-to-people contact, which he said could become “defining for our relations and serve as social and cultural bridges between the two countries”.

The DPM said the two sides had also discussed labour mobility.

“We agreed to continue work on legal pathways for Pakistan’s skilled manpower, expressing the need to combat human smuggling and illegal migration. Both sides agreed that by providing safe, orderly and regular migration channels, we not only protect migrants’ rights and lives but also dismantle the illegal model of smuggling networks,” he elaborated.

Dar further said that both Pakistan and Norway shared a commitment to multilateralism, the principles of the United Nations Charter, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity and the peaceful settlement of disputes.

“Our two countries remain actively engaged on issues related to the UN Security Council, and the two sides have strong convergence of views on major issues.

“Building on our previous experience of working together in international bodies and multilateral fora, both sides affirm their desire to continue mutual support and consultations on such forums.”

Dar said he had also briefed the Norwegian foreign minister and delegation on the Kashmir issue. He said he told them that India had added a new dimension to an already volatile security situation by unilaterally announcing the abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty in contravention of international law.

“We reiterate that India must end the weaponisation of water and uphold its treaty obligations under international legal obligations,” he asserted.

Dar said he had further briefed the Norwegian foreign minister on Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts for promoting dialogue, de-escalation and peaceful settlement of the US-Iran conflict. He thanked him for appreciating Pakistan’s role as a mediator in the conflict.

Moreover, he said, he had broadly discussed the Makkah defence pact with the visiting dignitary. “We had a great discussion, and it happens that all three countries enjoy the best of relations with Norway,” he said.

The DPM concluded his address, saying: “We agreed on the need to find peaceful solutions to the international conflicts in full respect of the principles of international law and the UN Charter.

“I thank his excellency, my dear friend, for his visit. I am confident that this visit will open a new chapter in Pakistan-Norway relations and will contribute to greater cooperation and mutual prosperity for the people of both countries in the years ahead.”

Delegation-level talks

Earlier in the day, Eide held delegation-level talks with DPM Dar, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

During the talks, the two sides reviewed the whole gamut of bilateral cooperation in various fields, including trade, investment, climate change, maritime affairs and education. They recognised the important role of the Pakistani diaspora in Norway and agreed to strengthen people-to-people ties between the two countries.

The two sides expressed satisfaction at the warm and cordial state of Pakistan-Norway relations and agreed to further deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest,” it said.

FO said the two sides also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments of mutual interest.

During the delegation-level talks, the visiting dignitary also recognised Pakistan’s role in the US-Iran war as “important and constructive”, lauding the leadership of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Munir and DPM Dar, as per the FO statement.

Eide had also appreciated Pakistan’s efforts to promote peace and expressed Norway’s desire to further strengthen bilateral ties earlier in the day in televised remarks.

He said Norway and Pakistan had a “very strong bilateral partnership”, adding that the presence of a large Pakistani community in Norway, which was “well integrated into Norwegian society”, had helped strengthen ties between the two countries.

“There are many leading politicians in Norway and many close colleagues who are actually of Pakistani-Norwegian descent, so it has really made a mark,” he said.

Eide said business ties between the two countries were also growing, particularly in the energy and fertiliser sectors, with Norwegian companies increasingly looking at opportunities in Pakistan.

He said Norway also saw opportunities for Pakistan to strengthen economic relations through its cooperation with Switzerland and Iceland, noting that the three countries could provide further avenues for expanding business relations.

Turning to the regional situation, Eide strongly commended the actions taken by Pakistan’s leadership.

Eide described the ongoing war as “incredibly dangerous” for global peace as well as the world economy, and praised Pakistan for stepping forward. He also appreciated Pakistan’s role in facilitating the Islamabad talks and maintaining engagement with the parties involved.

“I think it is fair to say that the position of Pakistan on the world stage, also in peacemaking, has really been strengthened by this commitment,” he said.

Eide said Norway was ready to assist Pakistan’s peace efforts, noting that Oslo had experience in peace negotiations and maintained open dialogue with both Tehran and Washington.

“Wherever we can be useful, we will,” he said.

He also highlighted Norway’s experience in international maritime affairs, saying the country was among the world’s major seafaring nations despite its relatively small population.

He said Norway could therefore play a constructive role in discussions concerning international maritime law and developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

Dar, Eide discuss bilateral ties

The two ministers also held a “restricted-format meeting” earlier today, FO said.

“DPM Dar warmly welcomed Eide to Pakistan. The two ministers discussed the full range of bilateral relations, as well as regional and international developments, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation in all areas of mutual interest,” according to FO.

Upon his arrival in Islamabad, Eide was received at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary (Europe) Ambassador Ayesha Ali.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FO said the minister is undertaking the visit from Aug 13-14 at Dar’s invitation.

The visit is the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade, the FO said, adding that the visit would build on high-level engagement between the two countries, including phone conversation between Dar and Eide in March and April, and the visit of Norway’s State Secretary Andreas Motzfeldt Kravik to Islamabad in May.

The FO stated that the visit would provide an opportunity to “further strengthen the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and Norway and to explore new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation”.

World.title: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia will form political, military mechanisms to coordinate under defence pact, Ankara says
World.content:
Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia will form political and military mechanisms under a defence pact signed between the regional powers last week, Turkiye’s defence ministry said on Thursday, adding the alliance would also deepen defence industry cooperation.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed last week as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Israeli war on Iran , which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

At a weekly briefing in Ankara, the ministry said the mechanisms would include the three countries’ defence ministers, foreign ministers, and military chiefs.

It added that the joint military exercises were also being planned under the pact, while cooperation could include joint production and technology sharing in the defence industry.

The remarks come a day after Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said that he hoped more countries would join the agreement.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily.

“Rather, we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

World.title: AJK police claim JAAC 'abducted' 8 highway police personnel on election duty
World.content:
Azad Jammu Kashmir (AJK) police said on Thursday that eight highway police personnel on election duty had been “abducted” by the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).

Addressing a televised press conference, police spokesperson Khawar Ali Shaukat alleged that the JAAC attacked security forces deputed on election duty in the region.

“Eight highway police officials on election duty were abducted,” he said as state media shared a collage of the officials’ pictures.

“The personnel are in the custody of JAAC and have been subjected to brutal abuse,” he said. He said that the “miscreants also threatened the families of the personnel that they would be martyred if their demands were not met”.

He said that recent events showed that the JAAC was not a peaceful group, but a violent one intent on challenging the state’s writ and weakening institutions.

“I want to make it clear that the state was not and is not weak. The state has always shown restraint,” he said, adding that violent acts for the sake of rights were not above the law.

He said that the people of the region, by participating in polls in the region, had made it clear that they had nothing to do with the proscribed group. He appealed to the public to disassociate themselves from the JAAC and to not get involved in acts where the state’s writ was challenged.

He appealed to parents to keep an eye on their children, saying: ““They play with the future of young people and instigate them against state through misleading propaganda and provocative statements.”

At the end of his press conference, he called on the JAAC to free the abducted personnel.

“The state will not accept any pressure with regards to the lives of these officials. If the personnel are harmed, obstacles are created in their release or threats to their families continue, the state will not show any leniency,” he said.

“If the state’s writ is challenged and if state officials are subjected to violence … the state will carry out its duties in accordance with the law and the Constitution,” he said, vowing strict action against such elements.

“Any group that challenges the state’s writ will be dealt with accordingly,” he said.

The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot and Mirpur on July 28, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Amid the tensions, elections are being held across the region in phases.

The government has accused militant elements “pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the unrest.

Last week, AJK Information Secretary Muhammad Rashid Hanif said that seven law enforcement personnel, including those from police and Rangers, were martyred during recent unrest in the region.

World.title: Body of missing Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi recovered on Broad Peak
World.content:
The body of Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, who was among the 10-person expedition that went missing after the deadly Broad Peak avalanche, was recovered and shifted to the mountain’s base camp, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said on Thursday.

The avalanche struck on July 30, cutting off contact with the 10-member international expedition led by world-renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja on Broad Peak, one of the world’s highest mountains. Purja’s company later confirmed there were no survivors .

The bodies of seven climbers were found. However, the search for Sakhi, American climber Sarah Mallory Geis, and Nepalese climber Nawang Thindu Sherpa was suspended last week due to a risk of fresh avalanches.

On Thursday, ACP member Naila Kiani said that Sakhi’s body had been found. According to Naila, a team of local volunteers from Shigar, searching the area on their own initiative, found the remains, which were subsequently confirmed as those of Sakhi.

She said the volunteers — Muhammad Nadeem, Muhammad Bashir and Abuzar — first spotted the body and alerted others in the area. They, along with other volunteers, brought the body down from Camp 1 to the base camp.

ACP General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the body had been shifted to the Broad Peak Base Camp and would be airlifted to Skardu by Pakistan Army helicopters, weather permitting.

He said the bodies of two remaining climbers have not yet been recovered. Shigri said rescue efforts for the remaining climbers would resume once weather conditions improved and the area was deemed safe.

He said the local volunteers located Sakhi’s body at an altitude of 5,600 metres.

Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja along with six elite Nepali guides were also part of the expedition. Purja, who served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, had broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.

World.title: High-profile terrorist commander killed in Bannu IBO: DPO
World.content:
PESHAWAR: A highly wanted terrorist commander was killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) conducted by the Bannu police and the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), the district police confirmed on Thursday.

Bannu’s District Police Officer (DPO) Captain (retd) Muhammad Furqan Bilal confirmed the terrorist’s killing in a conversation with Dawn.

The DPO confirmed that the terrorist was identified as a high-profile commander, Naseer Muhammad alias Geedarh, who carried a Rs6 million bounty on his head.

According to a statement issued by the police, an operation is underway against terrorists in the jurisdiction of Domel Police Station under the supervision of DPO Bilal, involving both the Bannu district police and CTD teams.

The statement elaborated that the operation is being conducted in Akbar Ali Khan Kili, Sada Khel, Sadarwan and the adjoining areas, where police and CTD teams are carrying out targeted actions based on intelligence reports regarding the presence and movement of terrorists.

Search and surveillance operations are also underway in the area, while security has been further tightened in various parts of the Bannu township and Domel.

The police said further details of the operation and its progress would be shared after the ongoing operation was completed.

There has been a resurgence in terrorism in Pakistan since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in Kabul in 2021.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

On Monday, the district police, CTD and security forces conducted a joint IBO in the jurisdiction of the Miryan police station in Bannu, leading to the killing of an unidentified terrorist in an exchange of fire and the arrest of 10 suspected individuals.

Last week, a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an IBO in KP’s Hangu district. Separately, security forces killed a key terrorist commander identified as Jamidullah during an operation in Jani Khel area of Bannu, a security official said.

World.title: SHC orders formation of committee to probe HIV outbreak among children at Karachi hospital
World.content:
KARACHI: The Sindh High Court (SHC) directed the provincial government on Thursday to constitute a committee for an “independent, impartial and comprehensive” inquiry into the HIV outbreak among children at Karachi’s Kulsum Bai Valika Hospital.

A two-member SHC bench, headed by Justice Adnanul Karim Memon and comprising Justice Muhammad Jaffer Raza, issued the directive as it announced its reserved judgement on a plea seeking an independent inquiry, registration of a case and lifelong medical treatment as well as appropriate compensation for the affected children.

The outbreak was initially reported late last year, following which the Sindh government carried out screening at the Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI)-run hospital located in Karachi’s SITE area. According to data shared by the Sindh government, at least 78 children have been found infected with HIV at the hospital while a screening in the nearby area also confirmed 120 additional cases.

But Advocate Tariq Mansoor, the lawyer who moved the SHC on the matter, claimed in his petition filed in May that the total number of infected children is around 200.

The court observed in its order on the plea that the departmental proceedings and reports submitted so far had been “insufficient to determine the number of affected persons, the source and circumstances of transmission, compliance with infection-control protocols and the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, as well as the supervisory and individual responsibility of the officials concerned”.

Keeping this in view, the court deemed it necessary “in the interest of justice, transparency and public confidence that an independent fact-finding mechanism be constituted by the competent authority, without expressing any final opinion regarding the guilt or innocence of any individual”.

It directed that a committee, headed by the Sindh chief secretary, be constituted. The chief secretary should co-opt two senior officers not below the rank of BS-20 and “preferably having no direct administrative involvement in the affairs of the hospital or the proceedings under inquiry” to join the committee, the court order stated.

The court directed that the committee should determine:

The actual number and particulars of children and other patients who were found HIV-positive and who received treatment at the hospital during the relevant period

The source, circumstances and possible mode of transmission of HIV, based on available medical and scientific evidence

Whether any disposable syringe or other medical equipment was reused, improperly disposed of, inadequately sterilised or otherwise used in violation of the applicable law, rules, protocols or standard medical practice

The existence and implementation of infection-prevention and control protocols at the hospital

The procurement, supply, storage, distribution and use of auto-lock, auto-destruct or auto-break syringes and the relevant record

The role and responsibility of medical, nursing, technical, administrative and supervisory officials concerned

Whether any officer or official, by act or omission, failed to discharge a statutory, administrative or supervisory duty

The status and legality of the departmental proceedings already initiated against the 37 officials and whether such proceedings adequately address the actual responsibility of the persons concerned

Whether any provision of the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010, or any other applicable law has been violated and, if so, the persons responsible

The measures required for preventing recurrence of any such incident in the future

The court order further stated that the committee should be empowered to examine all relevant records, including medical and laboratory reports, screening data, procurement and stock registers, syringe records, duty rosters, infection-control and inspection reports, inquiry proceedings, CCTV footage where such incidents occurred in Sindh and other material necessary for an “objective determination, while affording a fair opportunity of hearing to any person against whom an adverse finding is proposed”.

The committee should submit its comprehensive report to the competent authority, as well as the SHC, within two months of its constitution, the order read. It elaborated that the report should identify “the factual position and, where supported by evidence, fixing responsibility and recommending appropriate departmental, statutory or criminal action pursuant to Section 7 of the Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010”.

Pending the inquiry, the Sindh chief secretary should ensure through the relevant departments and SESSI that all affected HIV-positive children and other identified patients receive “comprehensive, uninterrupted and appropriate medical treatment”, including medicines, investigations, counselling and follow-up care, entirely free of cost, at any institution of higher standard as medically appropriate, the court ruled.

“All such expenses shall be borne by the government/SESSI and shall not be recovered from the affected patients or their families, and the arrangement shall continue for as long as medically required,” the court directed.

Noting the “extraordinary circumstances of the case and the vulnerability of the affected children”, the court further directed the provincial chief secretary to determine and process the “entitlement of each affected child/ family to compensation, financial assistance or other lawful relief, strictly in accordance with the applicable statutory framework and government policy”.

The chief secretary should ensure that the process is completed expeditiously and without unnecessary hardship to the affected families, the order said.
